facts.subject: Magic
facts.text: Characters have 3 spell slots per level out of 4 available spells, and magic learned is permanent.

evidence.quote: You have 3 slots but 4 spells...once spell from each level will have to be negated. So choose wisely...otherwise you'll find yourself in a major slump since the magic you learn is permanent!

facts.subject: Corneria Inn
facts.text: The inn in Corneria is the cheapest place to rest and save.

evidence.quote: always save at the inn in Corneria. It's the cheapest for the same return.

facts.subject: Knight
facts.text: Upon becoming a Knight, the Fighter can use level 1 to 3 White Magic.

evidence.quote: Once he becomes a Knight he can use low level white magic(1-3), which becomes incredibly useful outside of battles.

facts.subject: Ninja
facts.text: Upon becoming a Ninja, the Thief gains increased attack power and can use low level Black Magic.

evidence.quote: once he becomes a Ninja, his attack power is increased significantly and he can begin to use low level black magic.

facts.subject: Corneria Castle
facts.text: Train outside around Corneria Castle to reach level 3 before proceeding to the upcoming battle.

evidence.quote: Stay outside around Corneria castle and start to gain your levels to 3, any higher you'll easily win the upcoming battle ahead.

facts.subject: Garland
facts.text: Garland has 106 HP, and the party can defeat him by having the White Mage heal, the Black Mage cast Fire, and the Red Mage cast Fire while others attack.

evidence.quote: Boss Battle: Garland       HP: 106...Have the white mage heal, the black mage user fire, the red mage use fire if he has it and the rest attack as normal.

facts.subject: Lute
facts.text: Princess Sara gives the party the Lute in the throne room of Corneria after Garland is defeated.

evidence.quote: Congratulations! You have saved the princess from Garland...you are automatically taken back to the the throne room of Corneria where you are given a Lute from the princess.

facts.subject: Bridge

The WarMech is a monster only found in the long corridor leading up to
    Tiamat...There is
    a 1-64 chance of encountering this guy...and if you meet him, I highly
    suggest you have levels of at least 35.

Now when you first enter the room, move two columns down and then two columns right and you will enter the long corridor(not that hard eh?). Be wary in this corridor though, you may encounter the Warmech and have your long journey come to an end right there and then.
Monster:    | Warmech
Location:   | Longer vertical Tower before Tiamat(1-64 chance of battle)

However, you are never safe on this causeway as
a being more powerful than even the Four Fiends prowls here!  It's name is
Warmech, a deadly creation of an age long past, who sports 1000 Hit Points
as well as some serious attacking ability and even worse firepower!  Take
quick strides across the narrow bridge as you progress, and hope that your
number is not called in the 1-64 chance of meeting this monstrosity!
Do be warned, that the toughest monster in the game, WarMech, makes this bridge his place of business.
Floor 5 of the Floating Castle has a 4.7% chance of spawning a Warmech as a random encounter.

of the square, you will have to step back up and battle the Wizards AGAIN!

the left.  Here, there will be some odd structure that looks like a throne, with 
a treasure chest in the middle...retrieve the CROWN from the treasure chest, and exit 
the cave.

facts.subject: Maximum Hit Points

there are two types of level ups: weak and strong.

For a weak level up, MHP goes up by [V/4]+1

facts.subject: Random Encounters
facts.text: A random battle counter starts between 50 and 255, decrementing by 6 per step on outside terrain, 5 per step in monster lairs, and 2 per step on a ship until reaching a negative value.

evidence.quote:
at the beginning of the previous combat, a random number x is generated where
x = (50..255).  for each step taken

-outside on desert,plains,forest,marsh,river	decrement x by 6
-inside of a cave,or other monster lair		decrement x by 5
-outside on a ship				decrement x by 2
-on a damage square in a monster lair, in
  the airship, in a seaport, or inside		leave x alone

when x<0, battle begins.

facts.subject: World Map
facts.text: The world map is a 256 by 256 grid subdivided into 64 distinct 32 by 32 enemy domains.

evidence.quote:
the world map in FF1 is a grid 256 units wide by 256 units tall.  Label each
square on this map using X,Y pseudo-cartesian coordinates: (0,0) is the first
grid sqare in the NW-most corner,  (0,255) is the square in the SW-most
corner, (255,255) is the square in the SE-most corner, etc...

the entire world map is subdivided into 64 smaller (32x32) domains

facts.text: Base values for derived stat H% are (initial value at LV 1) + (3 x (LV-1)) for Fi/Kn/Bb/Ma, + (2 x (LV-1)) for Th/Ni/Rm/Rz, and + (LV - 1) for Wm/Wz/Bm/Bz.

evidence.quote:

   = (initial value at LV 1) + (LV - 1) for Wm/Wz/Bm/Bz

facts.subject: Magic Damage

evidence.quote:
every magical or special attack that does damage has a base power, call it M.
From this, the actual damage done = ([M/4]..M).  This damage cannot be
absorbed with armor.  If the target is resistant to the attack, damage done =
([M/8]..[M/4])*.  If the target is weak against the attack, damage done =
([3M/8]..[3M/2]).  Magical and special attacks which inflict damage never miss

facts.subject: Magic Spells
facts.text: Eligibility to buy a magic spell is determined by character class, with combat-only spells marked Cb and non-combat spells marked nC.

evidence.quote:
the capability to buy a particular magic spell for use in casting is
determined by character class.  The classes which are eligible to learn the 
spell are listed in the 'Who' column.  Some spells have different effects
based on whether combat is ensuing or not.  'Cb' in the 'Use' column means
that the described effect only happens if the spell is cast in combat.  'nC'
means that the effect only happens outside of combat.

facts.subject: Strength
facts.text: Characters gain 1 Damage for every two points of Strength.

evidence.quote:
This stat will help determine your Damage total when attacking, with 
characters gain 1 Damage for every two points of Strength.

facts.subject: Agility
facts.text: Agility helps determine a character's Evade% alongside the heaviness of their equipped armor.

evidence.quote:
This stat has the honour of helping to determine your Evade%, along with the
heaviness of your Armor.

facts.subject: Intelligence
facts.text: Intelligence has no discerned effect on spell power or magical defense.

evidence.quote:
it does not seem to have an
effect on the strength of spell power (which appears to be randomized), and
characters cannot make changes mid-battle form your commands (so no rating
an AI with this stat either).  It also does not appear to have any bearing
upon Magical Defense as suggested previously, thanks to some extra info from
the Final Fantasy board at GameFAQs.

facts.subject: Vitality
facts.text: Every four points of Vitality grants an additional Hit Point at each level gain.

evidence.quote:
This stat helps determine your overall Hit Point totals, with every four 
points of Vitality brings the gain of an additional Hit Point at each level.

facts.subject: Luck
facts.text: When running, a character's Luck is compared to the status byte of the character two positions lower, whereas the bottom two characters compare against a random value.

evidence.quote:
When running, a character's Luck is 
compared to the status byte of the character two positions lower, where as
the two bottom-rank characters are compared to a random value to determine
their running ability.

facts.subject: Damage
facts.text: The Damage stat is calculated by taking half of the Strength stat and adding the damage rating of the equipped weapon.

evidence.quote:
This stat is derived from your Strength stat that is cut in half and added
to the damage rating of your equipped weapon.

facts.subject: Hit%
facts.text: The Hit% stat determines both attack accuracy and the quantity of hits landed in a single attack.

evidence.quote:
This stat will determine the accuracy of a character's attack as well as the
quantity of hits they can land in one attack.

facts.subject: Absorb
facts.text: Absorb reduces damage taken from attacks and is calculated from all equipped armor, though if Absorb exceeds the incoming attack damage, the loss is still 1 Hit Point rather than 0.

evidence.quote:
This stat determines how much damage a character takes if an opponent lands
a blow.  The stat is determined by combining the Absorb stat all of the
equipped Armor on a character, BUT the Black Belt/Master has a bug where
their Absorb will be equal to their level (although their equipment will
retain any special defensive bonuses they contained).  If your Absorb is
higher than that of the Damage attack of your attacker, the resulting Hit
Point loss will always be 1 Hit Point, so no 0 damage will ever be taken.

facts.subject: Black Belt/Master
facts.text: Due to a bug, the Absorb of a Black Belt or Master is equal to their level.

evidence.quote:
BUT the Black Belt/Master has a bug where
their Absorb will be equal to their level (although their equipment will
retain any special defensive bonuses they contained).

facts.subject: Evade%
facts.text: Evade% determines whether an enemy successfully lands an attack on a character and may influence how many hits land.

evidence.quote:
This stat will determine if an enemy hits an attack on your character or
not.  It may also play a role in how many hits an enemy can land on your
character.

facts.subject: Fighter
facts.text: The Fighter features high Strength and Hit Points and can equip nearly every type of weapon and armor, but cannot cast magic.

evidence.quote:
The Fighter will be your big bad front man for any team you have.  He has
high Strength, Hit Points, and he can also equip nearly every type of Armor
and Weapon you find along the journey.  However, this character does have
the downside of no magic to call upon, but do you really need to cast spells
when you have a very dangerous weapons user anyway?

facts.subject: Knight
facts.text: The Knight can equip even more weapons and armors than the Fighter and gains the ability to cast Level 1-3 White Magic spells.

evidence.quote:
The Knight is an improved version of the Fighter in a few ways, mainly in
his use of even MORE weapons and armors than before!  Add onto that the
ability to use low level White Magic charges (Levels 1-3), and you have a
nearly unkillable force, protected by great armor, and the ability to do
some self healing.

facts.subject: Black Belt
facts.text: The Black Belt uses no magic, can equip very little armor, and attacks with fists rather than weapons to deal high damage.

evidence.quote:
The Black Belt starts out as a decent attacker who misses a fair bit when he
attacks, but blossoms into a machine of flying fists once he levels high
enough.  He has no use of magic at all, he can equip very little armor, but
he does gain some fairly good Hit Points (although not as much as the
Fighter unless really high levels are reached).

facts.subject: Master
facts.text: Promoting a Black Belt to Master grants no immediate stat gains and results in worse Magical Defense progression.

evidence.quote:
When upgraded to a Master, a Black Belt gains... ABSOLUTELY NOTHING!... It has also been 
brought to my attention that the Master actually develops WORSE Magical 
Defense than the Black Belt (see the Magical Defenses in the Bug/Oddities
section for more details).

facts.subject: Thief
facts.text: The Thief has poor weapon choices but can run away from battles at a higher success rate than the party lead.

evidence.quote:
The Thief is an interesting character to choose because he is an odd
character.  He has decent strength, decent Hit Points, and a moderate Hit%,
but he has such horrendous weapon choices that he deals little damage.  His
main (ie only) skill as a Thief is his ability to run away from battles at a
slightly more successful rate than your character in front of the party
(usually the position of a character determines their running ability).

facts.subject: Ninja
facts.text: The Ninja can equip nearly every weapon and armor and can cast Level 1-4 Black Magic spells, including Fast.

evidence.quote:
The Ninja gains the abilities of equipping nearly every
weapon and armor you come across as well as learning some low level Black
Magic spell charges (Level 1-4, including the highly useful Fast spell).

facts.subject: Red Mage
facts.text: The Red Mage can equip fairly good weapons, armors, and both White and Black Magic, but lacks high-end spells beginning at Level 5.

evidence.quote:
Red Mage is the jack of all trades, with the abilities to equip fairly good
weapons, armors, and both types of Magic.... He does
suffer from a lack of high end Magic spells, beginning at Level 5.

facts.subject: Red Wizard
facts.text: The Red Wizard can use better equipment and higher magic such as Life and Exit, but cannot learn Level 8 spells.

evidence.quote:
The Red Wizard is kind of an expansion of the earlier class to include
better weapons and armors, and even some higher magic (like Life and Exit).
However, he can not reach the Level 8 spells no matter how strong he is, but
this is a small price to pay for a well-rounded warrior.

facts.subject: White Mage
facts.text: The White Mage is restricted in weapon and armor choices and deals poor damage, but provides healing and defensive magic.

evidence.quote:
The White Mage is a limited weapons and armor user who can not be counted on
in battle to deal damage.  That said, this character shines through in those
tough battles where some extra defense is needed or some dire Curing
emergency.

facts.subject: White Wizard
facts.text: The White Wizard gains access to Level 6 and higher White Magic spells, including Cur4, Lif2, Wall, Exit, and Fade.

evidence.quote:
When the White Wizard rolls around to join the group, you will not gain many
new armor or weapon abilities, but Level 6 and higher spells will become
available to this specialist, including: Cur4, Lif2, Wall, Exit,  and Fade.

facts.subject: Black Mage
facts.text: The Black Mage has the lowest Hit Points of all characters and limited equipment, but uses offensive and status magic.

evidence.quote:
The Black Mage is a limited weapons and armor user who cannot be counted on
in battle to deal damage physically.  However, this little pointy hat toting
fellow can buy himself attacks spells to dole out the damage as well as
spells to disable the enemy or enhance his allies abilities.  He gets the
lowest Hit Points of all of the characters.

facts.subject: Black Wizard
facts.text: The Black Wizard can equip the Catclaw weapon and learn Black Magic up to Level 8, including Nuke.

evidence.quote:
Otherwise, more Black
Magic can be learned (right up to Level 8), including the godly Nuke spell.
The Catclaw is also available for a very dependable weapon, so the attacking
abilities will be increased.

   thereby giving the total amount of Hit Points lost.  Note that more
   Absorb than Damage dealt will result in a  1 Hit Point loss.

facts.subject: Running

positions down.

Gold: 2000

facts.subject: Titan

evidence.quote:
Head up and then left to find the Titan blocking the path.  He demands a
RUBY, and you just so happen to have found after creaming the Vampire!  Now
you may pass through, so head left and then down the windy path to find a
room.
Upon entering feed (give) your Ruby to the Titan and he will let you pass.

When you talk to the Titan with the Ruby in your possession, he'll take it from 
you, eat it (!), and then allow you free passage from now on.

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Lich has 400 HP, yields 3000 Gold and 2200 Exp., and acts as the Fiend of Earth on the final floor of the Earth Cave.

evidence.quote: BOSS BATTLE: Lich      HP: 400

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Lich is an undead enemy who can stun with physical attacks, cast Ice2 and Slep, but is extremely weak to Fire and Harm spells such as Fir3 and Hrm3.

evidence.quote:
Lich is the first fiend so he is of course the weakest of the four.  However,
he does have a fairly good attack power (he can stun the person he attacks),
spells like Ice2 (hits your entire party) and Slep (can knock members out of
the fight for a while), and he can land multiple hits as well.  That being
said, Lich is classified as undead, so Fire and harm spells will slaughter
his Hit points (therefore he can die from one blast each of Fir3 and Hrm3).

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Lich has a high Absorb rating against weapons, so battles rely either on Mages casting Fire and Harm or having Red and Black Mages cast Fast on weapon users.

evidence.quote:
Have your Mages go all out and cast Fire and Harm, leaving your
weapon users to remove meager amounts of Hit Points (Lich DOES have a high
Absorb rating), OR have your Red Mage and Black Mage cast Fast on the
weapon users to take him down physically

facts.subject: Earth Crystal
facts.text: Touching the altar protected by Lich causes the Earth ORB to shine, and the warp behind it returns the party to the outside world.

evidence.quote:
After defeating the fiend, step forward to touch the altar that he was
protecting, which will cause an ORB to shine!  Now continue forward to use
the warp there to return to the outside world!

facts.subject: Melmond
facts.text: Sailing south from Melmond to the peninsula's tip, turning west to land, sailing down the coast to a port, and hiking southwest then east leads to Crescent Lake.

evidence.quote:
Head south from Melmond and follow the
peninsula to it's tip, followed by turning west to follow that direction
until you reach land.  Now steer your Ship down the coast slightly to find a
port to land at.  You will now have to hike into Crescent Lake, so head
southwest to find Crescent Lake.  Now you should head east underneath the
lake, followed by cutting east to enter into the town itself.

facts.subject: Circle of Sages
facts.text: Speaking to the Sage located two spots to the right of where you enter the Circle of Sages rewards the party with the CANOE.

evidence.quote:
Head up through town to pass between the two Magic Shops,
and then head right through the twisting path to find the Circle of Sages.
Talk to each of them to learn various facts (some useful, some utterly
useless) about the Four Fiends, and be sure to visit the Sage two to the
right of the spot you enter the Circle to receive the CANOE!  Now your party
will have the ability to travel down rivers to reach previously inaccessible
areas!
One of the Sages gives you a Canoe which you can use to get to the Volcano.
Now it's time to talk go to the Circle of Sages.  They will tell you some semi-important information, but the real thing you're after is the CANOE.

facts.subject: Castle of Ordeals
facts.text: The recommended path is to journey first to the Castle of Ordeals in the north, then to the Ice Cave, and finally to Gurgu Volcano.

evidence.quote:
The first place to journey to will be the Castle of Ordeals in the
     north, then the Ice Cave, and finally onto Gurgu Volcano (this is the
     path I recommend and follow for this FAQ, but it is not a mandatory
     decision).

facts.subject: Castle of Ordeals
facts.text: To reach the Castle of Ordeals, sail north past the Power Peninsula, head west until north of the Temple of Fiends, sail north along the western coast, enter a small river leading inland by Canoe, and walk south to the castle.

evidence.quote:
Once you are ready, it is time to move west until you
are just to the north of the Temple of Fiends (use your B + SELECT to see
the World Map).  Once you are there, head north until you hit some land.
You will then go north along the western coast of this land mass, and you
will soon see a Castle to the east, surrounded by marsh (this is your goal).
Continue north along the coast until you find a small river leading inland,
which is where you will disembark from your ship as you Canoe south on the
river.  Leave the river when it bends and continue south on foot until you
reach the Castle of ordeals

facts.subject: CROWN
facts.text: Showing the old man the CROWN is required to enter the upper levels of the Castle of Ordeals to prove your courage.

evidence.quote:
Move forward to show the old man your CROWN as it is required for entering
the upper levels of the Castle to prove your courage.

facts.subject: Throne
facts.text: Stepping onto the throne in the upper-right corner of the floor starts the journey through the Castle of Ordeals.

evidence.quote:
Head to the up-right corner of the floor and set foot onto the
throne to start your journey!

facts.subject: Pillar Maze
facts.text: To navigate the teleportation floor, touch the single pillar in rooms one and two, the bottom pillar in room three, the single pillar in room four, the bottom pillar in room five, the single pillar down the hall in room six, and the right pillar in room seven.

evidence.quote:
The first
two rooms have one pillar only, so go touch them to warp forward.  The third
room has two, so choose the bottom one.  The fourth room has one choice,
which leads to the fifth room that has two (choose the bottom one).  The
sixth room is a long hall leading down to a single pillar, which is followed
by room seven where the right pillar is the one to choose to advance.

facts.subject: MUDGOL
facts.text: Mudgols have 176 HP, yield 800 Gold and 1257 Exp, have no real weak point, and can cast Fast.

evidence.quote:
They
have a high damage stat, and that can be furthered by their special ability
of using Fast!  They have no real weak point so attack them with your
weaponry and strongest Magic attacks to take them down before they can use
their brutal attacking abilities.

facts.subject: Zeus Gauntlet
facts.text: The treasure chest behind the Mudgol fight contains the Zeus Gauntlet, which casts Lit2 when used as an item in battle.

evidence.quote:
open up the Treasure Chest to
find the Zeus Gauntlet, which is not only a good Gauntlet for a
Fighter/Knight, Red Wizard, or Ninja, but it also has the honour of being
the first Weapon/Armor that you have found that can be used as an Item in
battle and have an effect.  When used as an Item, it will cast Lit2 every
time!

facts.subject: Stairs to Next Floor
facts.text: Leaving the Zeus Gauntlet room, taking the path down on the left, and touching the lower pillar warps the party to the room with the stairs leading to the next floor.

evidence.quote:
Now head out the door, take the path down ON THE LEFT (not the one
directly below the door), and then touch the lower pillar of the two here
to appear in the room with the stairway leading to the next floor!

their only special ability is

facts.subject: ZOMBIE DRAGON

evidence.quote: Watch for the treasure chest near the chair, it's protected by Zombie Dragon(s). Defeat the Dragons by using the Hrm3 spell(if you have it) and Fire3(if you have it) and have the rest of your fighters attack as normal.

You will have to brawl with a couple undead Dragons that have a high attack
power (they can also stun your fighters with their attack)!  Since they are

facts.subject: Throne

Once you have had your fill of the Zombie D's, step forward

facts.subject: Ice Cave
facts.text: To reach the Ice Cave by Canoe, follow the river stream to the northwest branch, turn east past the upward fork, head south into the west fork, disembark onto dry land, and head east and north.

evidence.quote:
Follow the stream till the branch appears, taking the northwest route.
Follow that current route, turning east and following it east past the fork
leading up.  Head south to take the west fork, and then follow that waterway
to dry land once again.  Head east and then north to find the entrance of
the Ice Cave!

facts.subject: Ice Cave
facts.text: Before exploring the Ice Cave, bring 99 Heal Potions and around 5 to 15 Soft Potions to survive damaging floors, status killers, and one-hit killers.

evidence.quote:
Far and away the toughest challenge yet, this cave will bring lots of heavy
hitters, damaging floor sections, undead stunners, status killers, and one
hit killers.  Bring 99 Heal Potions, around 5 to 15 Soft Potions, and your
ability to run as much as possible so you can to get through alive!

evidence.quote:
Head right from the entrance along the top wall, cutting down when the
passage opens up below, and then cut left to find a stairway leading
downwards.

facts.subject: healing potion
facts.text: Healing potions restore 30 HP per potion, and the player can carry a limit of 99 healing potions.

evidence.quote: The limit of 99 healing potions was a major bummer given that a Knight with virtually no HP left could take almost all of them to restore his HP at 30 per potion.

facts.subject: Magic
facts.text: Spells are divided into levels from Level 1 up to level 8, with 9 being the maximum charges that can be used per spell level.

evidence.quote: Each spell was divided into a level of magic with Fire and Lightning being Level 1 spells, as to Nuke being a level 8 spell. Each spell level could only be used so many times before it would be used up. 9 was the max times which you could use any of the spells in each level, but they had to be worked up from 0 to 9.

facts.subject: Magic
facts.text: Magic spells must be bought in stores, costing from 100 gold for a level 1 spell up to 60,000 gold for a level 8 spell.

evidence.quote: Magic also had to be bought in the various stores, which shouldn't have been a problem except the huge amount of gold that they started to cost (100 gold per level 1 spell to 60,000 gold per level 8 spell) when that could be spent towards outfitting your party with weapons and armor and healing potions.

facts.subject: Final Fantasy

evidence.quote: As for the downside of Final Fantasy, I didn't like the fact that on the original cartridge you could only have one save game at any given time.

facts.subject: Town of Melmond
facts.text: Melmond lacks an Item Shop and a Clinic, requiring players to stock up on potions in Elfland and travel back to revive fallen allies.

evidence.quote:
Before heading any further, you'll have to head back to Elfland and buy
some Houses and Soft Potions along with Cabins, Pure and Heal Potions
if you need them as there isn't an Item Shop in Melmond. Also be
warned, there is not a Clinic here either, so you'll have to travel
back in order to revive defeated members.

Note that there is no Item Shop in Melmond, so you will have to 
return to either Elfland or Coneria to buy Heal Potions.

facts.subject: Floor 2
facts.text: Navigating the pillar teleporter maze requires entering the bottom pillar when faced with top and bottom, the solo pillar, the bottom pillar at the southwestern corner, the south solo pillar, the right pillar at the northwestern corner, and finally the second pillar furthest down past the Zeus Gauntlet room to reach the staircase to Floor 3.

evidence.quote:
When there are two
pillars, one at the top and the other at the bottom of the room, enter
the bottom pillar, and then you'll be at a lone pillar, so enter that
one. You will now be at the southwestern corner of the room, with a
choice of of a top and bottom pillar to enter...while the
bottom pillar will lead to a new location. Follow the lone path on
which you just came all the way south to a solo pillar and enter it.
You will now be up in the northwestern corner of the floor, with two
more pillars to choose from, either right or left...where as the right pillar will lead
you further along in the maze...It is the second pillar and also the furthest one down from the
room with the Zeus Gauntlet in it...Upon entering the correct
pillar, you will be in the southeastern corner of the floor, next to a
staircase leading up to Floor 3.

facts.subject: Imps and Wolves
facts.text: Grassy areas outside Coneria feature encounters with Imps, Wolves, and occasionally Madponies.

evidence.quote: Walk around on the green grass just outside Coneria until you get attacked...You'll fight mainly Imps and Wolves, although perhaps you may encounter Madponies.

facts.subject: Inn
facts.text: Saving at the Coneria Inn costs 30 gold.

evidence.quote: When you finally have everything, save your game at the Inn (it costs 30 gold) and prepare to head to the Temple of Fiends.

facts.subject: Tent
facts.text: Tents cost 75 gold each and allow saving outdoors on the world map.

evidence.quote: Item Shop [Heal Potion 60 GP] [Pure Potion 75 GP] [Tent 75 GP]
If you want, you can save up to buy a couple of Tents (75 gold each), so you can save your game right outside the Temple, but you don't have to.

facts.subject: Cap
facts.text: A chest in the bottom-left room of the Temple of Fiends contains a Cap.

evidence.quote: You start off at the bottom-center of the Temple. In the bottom-left is a Cap.

facts.subject: Cabin and Heal Potion
facts.text: Chests in the top-left room of the Temple of Fiends contain a Cabin and a Heal Potion.

evidence.quote: In the top-left is a Cabin and a Heal Potion.

facts.subject: Treasuries
facts.text: The top-right and bottom-right doors in the Temple of Fiends are locked and require the Mystic Key to open.

evidence.quote: In the top-right and bottom-right are locked doors, which you will need that Mystic Key for.

facts.subject: Garland
facts.text: Garland has 106 HP and attacks physically in the center room of the Temple of Fiends.

evidence.quote:
Garland is in the center room, which you must enter from the bottom.  When you talk to him, he insults you, and then attacks.

BOSS - GARLAND
HP: 106  

He's not very difficult, all he uses is physical attacks.

facts.subject: Garland
facts.text: Garland can be defeated using physical attacks alongside the Black Mage's Fire or Lit spells.

evidence.quote: Your fighting types should just pound away on him.  The White Mage should act as the healer, utilizing the Cure Spell.  The Black Mage should not fight, but instead use Fire or Lit on Garland.

facts.subject: Princess Sara
facts.text: Talking to Princess Sara after defeating Garland teleports the party back to Coneria Castle.

evidence.quote: When you beat him, talk to Princess Sara.  She'll thank you and then teleport you back to Coneria Castle.

facts.subject: King of Coneria
facts.text: The King builds a bridge to the north after Princess Sara is rescued.

evidence.quote: Talk to the King.  He'll tell you that he ordered a bridge built to the north, allowing you access to the rest of this continent.

facts.subject: Princess Sara
facts.text: Princess Sara gives the Light Warriors a Lute upon speaking to her at Coneria Castle.

evidence.quote:
Sara will show her undying gratitude to the Light Warriors by
bestowing a fabulous gift upon them!  Gold?  Jewels? Her hand in marriage?
NO!  You get an old, beat up, barely holding together LUTE!
If you talk to the Princess, she also thanks you for saving her, and gives you the Lute, which she says has been passed down from Queen to Princess for 2000 years and it may come in handy.
Talk to the Princess.  She will give you a Lute.

facts.subject: Lute
facts.text: A man on the first floor of Coneria Castle states that the Lute can break the evil gate.

evidence.quote: A man on the first floor will only tell you that the Lute can break the evil gate.

facts.subject: Matoya
facts.text: Townspeople in Coneria reveal that Matoya lives to the north and needs the Crystal to see due to poor eyesight.

evidence.quote: An old woman tells you that north of Coneria lives a witch named Matoya and a young lady will tell you that Matoya needs the Crystal to see because she has poor eyesight.

facts.subject: Matoya's Cave
facts.text: To reach Matoya's Cave from Coneria, cross the northern bridge, pass the port between two mountain ranges, and proceed through the forest around the river.

evidence.quote: A short distance north of Coneria is the bridge the King built...Continue north, passing by the port in between the two mountain ranges.  Then travel through the forest, around the river, and you'll see a cave.  This is Matoya's cave.

facts.subject: World Map
facts.text: A broom outside Matoya's room speaks backwards indicating 'PUSH B SELECT' to open the World Map.

evidence.quote: You'll see a broom outside the room.  Talk to it and it will say "TCELES B HSUP".  Read that message backwards.
When you get outside, hold B and push Select (the message the broom told you).  Presto!  The World Map appears.

A broom there will say HSUP B 
TCELES.  Read it backward to see the message "Push B Select"  Do this in the 
outer world to see a world map.

facts.subject: Matoya's Cave
facts.text: Two Heal Potions and a Pure Potion are found on the left side of Matoya's Cave by walking over the skulls.

evidence.quote: Go in the room and get the two Heal Potions and Pure Potion on the left side (you can walk over the skulls).
If you cross the bridge and keep heading straight north until you can't anymore, you'll bump into Matoya's Cave, which contains 3 chests with a Heal potion, another Heal potion, and a Pure potion.

facts.subject: Matoya
facts.text: Matoya explains that she was blinded because someone stole her Crystal.

evidence.quote: She will tell you that she has been blinded because someone has stolen her Crystal.

facts.subject: Pravoka
facts.text: To reach Pravoka from Matoya's Cave, head back around the river and forest, travel east at the mountains, and go south through a small desert and forest.

evidence.quote: To get to Pravoka, head back down through the forest and around the river again and go east at the mountains...You'll pass through a small desert and some more forest.  Follow it south until you find the town of Pravoka.

facts.subject: Inn
facts.text: The Inn in Pravoka costs 50 gold to heal and save.

evidence.quote: Before confronting the pirates, head directly north to the Inn (50 gold) to heal and save.

facts.subject: Pirate
facts.text: The pirate confrontation in Pravoka consists of nine Pirates with 6 HP each and rewards 360 gold.

evidence.quote:
Pirate  HP: 6

There are nine pirates, but they are easily beaten.  Just be careful of them ganging up one guy.  You'll get 360 gold from this battle, useful indeed.

facts.subject: Ship
facts.text: Talking to the pirate captain after defeating his nine crew members yields the Ship.

evidence.quote: Talk to the pirate after you've beaten his crew, and he'll relinquish his Ship.  Now you can take to the seas.

facts.subject: Ship
facts.text: Ships can dock only at ports, and there are no ports located in the northern part of the world.

evidence.quote: You'll learn that ships can stop only at ports, but there aren't any ports in the northern part of the world.

facts.subject: Elf Prince
facts.text: The Elven prince across the sea is under a sleeping spell and requires Matoya's Herb to awaken.

evidence.quote: You'll also learn that there are Elves across the sea, and their prince is under a sleeping spell and needs Matoya's Herb.

facts.subject: Fighter Equipment
facts.text: In Pravoka, the Fighter can buy Short Sword for 550 gold, Iron Armor for 800 gold, Wooden Shield for 15 gold, and Gloves for 60 gold.

evidence.quote: Fighter - Short Sword (550), Iron Armor (800), Wooden Shield (15), Gloves (60)

facts.subject: Thief Equipment
facts.text: In Pravoka, the Thief can buy Scimitar for 200 gold and Gloves for 60 gold.

evidence.quote: Thief - Scimitar (200), Gloves (60)

facts.subject: Red Mage Equipment and Magic
facts.text: In Pravoka, the Red Mage can buy Short Sword for 550 gold, Gloves for 60 gold, and Mute, Alit, and Ice spells for 400 gold each.

evidence.quote: Red Mage - Short Sword (550), Gloves (60), Mute (400), Alit (400), Ice (400)

facts.subject: White Mage Equipment and Magic
facts.text: In Pravoka, the White Mage can buy Gloves for 60 gold, and Mute, Alit, and Invs spells for 400 gold each.

evidence.quote: White Mage - Gloves (60), Mute (400), Alit (400), Invs (400)

facts.subject: Black Mage Equipment and Magic
facts.text: In Pravoka, the Black Mage can buy Gloves for 60 gold, and Ice and Slow spells for 400 gold each.

evidence.quote: Black Mage - Gloves (60), Ice (400), Slow (400)

facts.subject: Elfland
facts.text: To reach Elfland by sea, sail south along the Aldi Sea coastline to the south shore, head west to a port, and walk directly south through the forest.

evidence.quote: Head south along the coastline until you reach the shore on the south side.  Then head west until you see a port.  Directly south of this port through the forest is the village and castle of Elfland.

facts.subject: Astos
facts.text: Astos attacked Elfland Castle and cast a sleeping curse on the Prince, which only Matoya's Herb can break.

evidence.quote: Talking to the people here reveals that someone named Astos attacked the castle, putting the Prince under a sleeping curse.  The only thing that can wake him is Matoya's Herb.

facts.subject: Treasury
facts.text: The treasury around the right edge of Elfland Castle is locked with the Mystic Key.

evidence.quote: If you go around the right edge of the castle, you'll find the treasury.  Of course, it's been locked with the mystic Key.

facts.subject: Astos
facts.text: Astos is the Dark Elf who secludes himself in disguise.

evidence.quote: The townspeople here tell you that Astos is the Dark Elf.  He wears a disguise and secludes himself.

facts.subject: Ancient Castle
facts.text: An ancient castle with a spooky atmosphere is situated to the northwest of Elfland.

evidence.quote: Someone tells you there is an ancient castle to the northwest with a spooky air about it.

facts.subject: Dwarf Cave
facts.text: To reach the Dwarf Cave, sail west along the coast, turn north hugging the coast past a strip of land to a port, then proceed southwest on foot.

evidence.quote: Go west along the coast and then turn to the north and hug that coast...Keep going north until you find a port.  The Dwarf Cave is just a little ways to the southwest.

facts.subject: Astos
facts.text: Dwarves in the Dwarf Cave state that Astos stole Matoya's Crystal.

evidence.quote: A couple of them inform you that Astos also stole Matoya's Crystal.

facts.subject: Blacksmith
facts.text: The blacksmith in the Dwarf Cave promises to forge a legendary sword if brought Adamant.

evidence.quote: When you talk to the blacksmith, he'll tell you that he'll make you a legendary sword, but he requires Adamant.

facts.subject: Nerrick
facts.text: Nerrick the dwarf requires TNT to finish digging his canal.

evidence.quote: The dwarf named Nerrick is digging a canal, but he needs TNT to finish it.

facts.subject: Floater
facts.text: A dwarf in the Dwarf Cave mentions an item called a Floater that makes things float.

evidence.quote: Someone also tells you about something called a Floater, which, not surprisingly, makes things float.

facts.subject: Bracelets
facts.text: Bracelets provide the same protection as regular armor without reducing evade percentage.

evidence.quote: You also find out another important fact about armor, and that is that bracelets protect you as well as regular armor does.  It is more advantageous to wear a bracelet because it doesn't weigh you down like heavy armor does.  Therefore, you get the protection without your evade % suffering.

facts.subject: 1025 gold
facts.text: A treasure room directly north of the stairs in the Dwarf Cave contains 1025 gold.

evidence.quote: The room directly north of the stairs has 1025 gold in it.

facts.subject: South Room
facts.text: The room to the far south of the Dwarf Cave is locked with the Mystic Key.

evidence.quote: But the room to the far south is locked with that elusive mystic Key.

facts.subject: Gaia Magic Shop
facts.text: The Level 7 magic available includes Cur4 and Hrm4 for the White Wizard, and Ice3 and Brak for the Black Wizard.

evidence.quote: The Level 7 magic you want is Cur4 and Hrm4 for the White Wizard, and Ice3 and Brak for the Black Wizard.

facts.subject: Red Wizard
facts.text: The Red Wizard can only learn Ice3 among the Level 7 spells.

evidence.quote: The Red Wizard can only learn Ice3.

facts.subject: Gaia Magic Shop
facts.text: The Level 8 magic available includes Fade and Wall for the White Wizard, and Stop and Zap! for the Black Wizard.

evidence.quote: The Level 8 magic you want is Fade and Wall for the White Wizard, and Stop and Zap! for the Black Wizard.

facts.subject: Red Wizard
facts.text: The Red Wizard cannot learn any Level 8 magic.

evidence.quote: The Red Wizard can't learn any Level 8 magic.

facts.subject: Submarine
facts.text: A submarine created to go underwater requires Oxyale to run.

evidence.quote: One of the people has created a submarine to go underneath the sea to find the Mermaids, but it needs Oxyale to run.

facts.subject: Dr. Unne
facts.text: Dr. Unne needs a Slab to be able to teach the Lefeinish language.

evidence.quote: Dr. Unne needs a Slab to be able to teach the language.

facts.subject: Caravan
facts.text: The caravan master in the northern section of the western desert sells a Bottle for 50,000 gold.

evidence.quote: The caravan is in the northern section of this desert.  The master has for sale a "Bottle" priced at 50,000 gold.

facts.subject: Bottle
facts.text: Do not use the Bottle until returning to Gaia's spring, or the fairy will fly away and waste 50,000 gold.

evidence.quote: IMPORTANT:  DO NOT USE THE BOTTLE UNTIL YOU GET BACK TO GAIA'S SPRING.  If you do, the fairy will fly away and you'll have wasted 50,000 gold.

facts.subject: Gaia Pond
facts.text: Using the Bottle next to the pond in Gaia summons the fairy, who gives you Oxyale.

evidence.quote: Stand next to the pond and use the Bottle.  The fairy will appear and give you Oxyale.

facts.subject: Submarine
facts.text: Touching the submarine in Onrac while carrying Oxyale transports the party to the Sea Shrine.

evidence.quote: You can pass because you have Oxyale.  Touching the submarine transports you to the Sea Shrine.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 3rd Floor Western Room
facts.text: The western room on the 3rd floor contains 9900 gold.

evidence.quote: Western room:  9900 gold

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 3rd Floor Eastern Room
facts.text: The eastern room on the 3rd floor contains 2000 gold.

evidence.quote: Eastern room:  2000 gold

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 3rd Floor Northwestern Stairs
facts.text: Stairs in the northwestern corner of the 3rd floor lead down to the 2nd floor.

evidence.quote: Northwestern corner:  Stairs down to 2nd floor

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 3rd Floor Northeastern Stairs
facts.text: Stairs in the northeastern corner of the 3rd floor lead up to the 4th floor.

evidence.quote: Northeastern corner:  Stairs up to 4th floor

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 4th Floor Southwest Room
facts.text: Walking south and west on the 4th floor leads to a room containing 20 gold.

evidence.quote: Walk south and west (ignoring the first room you see) to find a room with 20 gold.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 4th Floor Northwest Room
facts.text: A room to the northwest on the 4th floor contains Opal Armor.

evidence.quote: Then walk northwest to find a room with Opal Armor.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 4th Floor Far South Room
facts.text: A room located as far south as possible on the 4th floor contains the Light Axe.

evidence.quote: Walk south as far as you can to find a room with the Light Axe.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 4th Floor Upper East Room
facts.text: Taking the upper eastern path on the 4th floor leads to a room containing the Mage Staff.

evidence.quote: Then walk east and take the upper path to find a room with the Mage Staff.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 4th Floor Lower East Room
facts.text: Taking the lower eastern path on the 4th floor leads to a room containing 12350 gold and stairs up to the 5th floor.

evidence.quote: Then go back and take the lower path to find a room with 12350 gold and also the stairs up to the 5th floor.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 5th Floor
facts.text: Among the treasures on the 5th floor of the Sea Shrine is the Slab needed by Dr. Unne.

evidence.quote: Among the numerous treasures you will get on this floor (including lots of Opal stuff), you will get the Slab that Dr. Unne needs.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 2nd Floor Northeast Stairs
facts.text: Stairs down to 3rd floor B are located in the northeast corner of the 2nd floor.

evidence.quote: The stairs down to 3rd floor B are in the northeast corner.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 3rd Floor B
facts.text: Stairs on 3rd floor B lead up to 4th floor B.

evidence.quote: 3rd floor B - Take the stairs up to 4th floor B.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 4th Floor B
facts.text: Stairs on 4th floor B lead down to 3rd floor C.

evidence.quote: 4th floor B - Take the stairs down to 3rd floor C.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 3rd Floor C Room
facts.text: The chests in the room on 3rd floor C contain 560 gold.

evidence.quote: The chests in the room contain 560 gold.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 3rd Floor C South Exit
facts.text: Stairs down to 2nd floor B are located just outside the south exit of the room on 3rd floor C.

evidence.quote: The stairs down to 2nd floor B are just outside the south exit of this room.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 2nd Floor B Southeast Room
facts.text: Following the intersection south and east on 2nd floor B leads to a room containing 15825 gold.

evidence.quote: Walk west until you reach an intersection, then go south and east to find a room with 15825 gold.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 2nd Floor B West Room
facts.text: Walking as far west as possible on 2nd floor B leads to a room with a Power Gauntlet and 5835 gold.

evidence.quote: Then walk as far west as you can to find a room with a Power Gauntlet and 5835 gold.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 2nd Floor B North Room
facts.text: Walking north on 2nd floor B leads to a room containing a Light Axe.

evidence.quote: Then walk to the north to find a room with a Light Axe.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 2nd Floor B East Room
facts.text: Walking east on 2nd floor B leads to a room containing a Ribbon and 19990 gold.

evidence.quote: Walk to the east to find a room with a Ribbon and 19990 gold.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine 2nd Floor B Northwest Stairs
facts.text: Stairs down to the 1st floor are located to the northwest on 2nd floor B.

evidence.quote: Finally, walk northwest to find the stairs down to the 1st floor.

facts.subject: Kraken
facts.text: Kraken has 800 HP, casts Lit2, and uses the special attack Ink to cause Dark.

evidence.quote:
BOSS:  KRAKEN
HP: 800
Magic:  Lit2
Special Attack:  Ink (Dark)

facts.subject: Kraken
facts.text: Lit3 is a very effective attack spell against Kraken, while Inv2 helps lessen his physical attacks of up to 8 hits.

evidence.quote: Kraken's physical strength is a threat (up to 8 hits per attack!), so use Inv2 to help you lessen that...Lit3 is a very effective attack spell to utilize.

facts.subject: Waterfall Entrance
facts.text: Canoeing north along the river next to Onrac leads to the waterfall.

evidence.quote: Go back to the river next to Onrac and canoe north until you find the waterfall, then enter it.

facts.subject: Waterfall Path
facts.text: Starting from the southeast corner of the Waterfall, follow the forks west, north, west, west, and then all the way south to reach the room.

evidence.quote: You start in the southeast corner of the maze.  Follow these directions for when you come to forks in the path:  west, north, west, west, then walk all the way south.

facts.subject: Robot
facts.text: The Robot inside the Waterfall room gives you the Cube to allow transfer to the Floating Castle.

evidence.quote: Inside the room is the Robot, who gives you the Cube, which he says will allow you to transfer to the Floating Castle.

facts.subject: Dr. Unne
facts.text: Talking to Dr. Unne in Melmond teaches you the language of the Lefeinish.

evidence.quote: Go talk to Dr. Unne in Melmond and he will teach you the language of the Lefeinish.

facts.subject: Lefein Landing
facts.text: To reach Lefein, land the Airship in a tiny patch of grass far to the north next to the mountains and walk south.

evidence.quote: There's a tiny little patch of grass far to the north (next to the mountains at the right side of the desert) and you have to land there and go far to the south to reach the town.

facts.subject: Lefeinish Inhabitant
facts.text: Someone in Lefein gives you the Chime so you can enter the Mirage Tower.

evidence.quote: The entrance to the Floating Castle is the Mirage Tower, which you can enter with the Chime.  Someone will give you that Chime so you can enter it.

facts.subject: Secret Magic Shop
facts.text: Walking east through the break in the trees in northeast Lefein reveals a secret Level 8 magic shop selling Lif2 and Nuke.

evidence.quote: Go through the break in the trees in the northeast part of the town and keep walking east.  You'll find a Level 8 magic shop which sells Lif2 and Nuke.

facts.subject: Mirage Tower 1st Floor Central Room
facts.object: Aegis Shield, Vorpal, Heal Helmet, Cabin, and 30040 gold
facts.text: Chests in the central room on the 1st floor of Mirage Tower contain the Aegis Shield, Vorpal, Heal Helmet, a Cabin, and 30040 gold.

evidence.quote: They contain the Aegis Shield, Vorpal, Heal Helmet, a Cabin, and 30040 gold.

facts.subject: Mirage Tower 2nd Floor Central Room
facts.object: Thor's Hammer, Sun Sword, Dragon Armor, House, and 59075 gold
facts.text: Chests in the central room on the 2nd floor contain Thor's Hammer, Sun Sword, Dragon Armor, a House, and 59075 gold.

evidence.quote: The treasures in the center are Thor's Hammer, Sun Sword, Dragon Armor, a House, and 59075 gold.

facts.subject: Blue Dragon
facts.text: A Blue Dragon is positioned right inside the room entrance on the 3rd floor of Mirage Tower.

evidence.quote: A Blue Dragon is right inside.

facts.subject: Floating Castle Transporter
facts.text: A Cube is required to operate the transporter on the 3rd floor of Mirage Tower leading to the Floating Castle.

evidence.quote: The robot will tell you that you need a Cube to operate the transporter.  This must be the one that goes to the Floating Castle.

facts.subject: Floating Castle 1st Floor Left Room
facts.text: The left room on the 1st floor contains a Heal Potion and 21950 gold.

evidence.quote: Left leads to a room with a Heal Potion and 21950 gold.

facts.subject: Floating Castle 1st Floor Down Room
facts.text: The room downwards on the 1st floor contains the Bane Sword.

evidence.quote: Down leads to a room with the Bane Sword.

facts.subject: Floating Castle 1st Floor Right Room
facts.text: The right room on the 1st floor contains a ProRing, Heal Helmet, and 11900 gold.

evidence.quote: Right leads to a room with a ProRing, Heal Helmet, and 11900 gold.

facts.subject: Floating Castle 2nd Floor Northeastern Room
facts.text: The northeastern room on the 2nd floor contains an Opal Gauntlet.

evidence.quote: Northeastern room:  Opal Gauntlet

facts.subject: Floating Castle 2nd Floor Eastern Room
facts.text: The eastern room on the 2nd floor contains a Ribbon and an Opal Shield.

evidence.quote: Eastern room:  Ribbon, Opal Shield

facts.subject: Floating Castle 2nd Floor Southeastern Room
facts.text: The southeastern room on the 2nd floor contains a White Shirt and a Black Shirt.

evidence.quote: Southeastern room:  White Shirt, Black Shirt

facts.subject: Floating Castle 2nd Floor Southwestern Room
facts.text: The southwestern room on the 2nd floor contains the Adamant.

evidence.quote: Southwestern room:  Adamant

facts.subject: Blacksmith
facts.text: Bringing the Adamant found on the 2nd floor to the blacksmith in Dwarf Cave allows him to forge the sword Xcalber for the Knight.

evidence.quote: The Adamant you find here is what the blacksmith in the Dwarf Cave needed.  Bring it to him and he will make the sword Xcalber, which your Knight can equip.

facts.subject: Floating Castle 2nd Floor Western Room
facts.text: The western room on the 2nd floor contains 13880 gold.

evidence.quote: Western room:  13880 gold

facts.subject: Floating Castle 2nd Floor Northwestern Room
facts.text: The northwestern room on the 2nd floor contains a Silver Helmet and a House.

evidence.quote: Northwestern room:  Silver Helmet, House

facts.subject: Window
facts.text: Examining the window on the 3rd floor reveals that the Four Forces are flowing into the center of the Four Altars, the Temple of Fiends.

evidence.quote: When you examine the window, you learn that the Four Forces are flowing into the center of the Four Altars, the Temple of Fiends.

facts.subject: Floating Castle 3rd Floor Northern Room
facts.text: The northern room on the 3rd floor contains a ProRing, a Heal Potion, and 14450 gold.

evidence.quote: Northern room:  ProRing, Heal Potion, 14450 gold

facts.subject: Floating Castle 3rd Floor Western Room
facts.text: The western room on the 3rd floor contains a Katana, a Soft Potion, and 7550 gold.

evidence.quote: Western room:  Katana, Soft Potion, 7550 gold

facts.subject: Floating Castle 3rd Floor Eastern Room
facts.text: The eastern room on the 3rd floor contains a ProCape, Cloth, a Soft Potion, and 24125 gold.

evidence.quote: Eastern room:  ProCape, Cloth, Soft Potion, 24125 gold

facts.subject: Floating Castle 4th Floor Path
facts.text: To reach the 5th floor teleporter on the repeating maze of the 4th floor, follow the directions: up, left, up, left.

evidence.quote: To reach the teleporter to the 5th floor, follow these directions: up, left, up, left.

facts.subject: WarMech
facts.text: There is a slight chance of encountering WarMech along the bridge on the 5th floor.

evidence.quote: There's a slight chance you'll have to fight WarMech, who is even more powerful than Tiamat.

facts.subject: Tiamat
facts.text: Tiamat has 1000 HP and uses special attacks Thunder, Poison Gas, and Blizzard.

evidence.quote:
BOSS:  TIAMAT
HP: 1000
SPECIAL ATTACKS:  Thunder, Poison Gas, Blizzard

facts.subject: Time Gate
facts.text: The Time Gate at the Temple of Fiends can be broken because the four Orbs shine once again, allowing travel back 2000 years in time.

evidence.quote: You must travel back 2000 years in time to confront this person by breaking the Time Gate at the Temple of Fiends.  It can be broken because the four Orbs shine once again.

facts.subject: Black Orb
facts.text: Approaching the black Orb in the center room allows you to cover it with the four Orbs and travel back 2000 years in time.

evidence.quote: Approach the Orb in the center room.  You will use the four Orbs to cover the black Orb, allowing you to travel back 2000 years in time.

facts.subject: Phantom
facts.text: A Phantom attacks as soon as you enter the center room on the 3rd floor.

evidence.quote: Enter the center room from the bottom.  You'll be attacked by a Phantom as soon as you enter.

facts.subject: Temple of Fiends 3rd Floor Center Room
facts.text: The treasure chests in the center room on the 3rd floor contain 110000 gold.

evidence.quote: The treasure chests contain 110000(!) gold.

facts.subject: Stone Plate
facts.text: Playing the Lute on the Stone Plate allows you to descend.

evidence.quote: Move to the Stone Plate on the floor.  No, the Rod doesn't work on this one.  The Lute does...Descend.

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Before descending the stairs to floor B2 in the lower right corner, you must defeat Lich once again.

evidence.quote: The stairs down to floor B2 are in the lower right corner.  However, before you can descend them you must fight the Fiend of the Earth, Lich, once again.

facts.subject: Floor B2
facts.text: On Floor B2, the stairs down to Floor B3 are adjacent to the start but require taking a circuitous route to reach.

evidence.quote:
Floor B2 - The stairs down to Floor B3 are right next to you, but you have to 
take the circuitous route to get to them.

facts.subject: Floor B2
facts.text: South of the stairs on Floor B2, entering the right door leads to a treasure chest containing a ProCape.

evidence.quote:
When you do reach the stairs, don't 
go down them at first; instead go south to the rooms down there.  Take the right 
door to find a treasure chest with a ProCape.

facts.subject: Floor B2
facts.text: Passing through the ProCape room on Floor B2 into the next room leads to a treasure chest with 26000 gold.

evidence.quote:
Go through this room and into the 
next to find a chest with 26000 gold.

facts.subject: Floor B2
facts.text: Taking the left door south of the stairs on Floor B2 leads to a treasure chest containing a ProRing.

evidence.quote:
Go back and take the left door to find a 
chest with a ProRing.

facts.subject: Floor B2
facts.text: Going through the ProRing room and down the next corridor on Floor B2 leads to a room with a Katana.

evidence.quote:
Go through this room and down the next corridor to find a 
room with a Katana.

facts.subject: Kary
facts.text: The Fiend of Fire, Kary, must be fought before taking the stairs down to Floor B3.

evidence.quote:
Go back and take the stairs down to Floor B3.  Of course, 
you'll have to fight the Fiend of Fire, Kary, before you can do that.

Travel
to the right then take the exit and head south then left to the stairs to get

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Lich is immune to Mute; defend against his spells using Aice, Alit, and Afir, and cast Fast on fighters while keeping Mages from physically attacking.

evidence.quote:
Mute does not work on him; he's too powerful.  So, 
instead, cast your anti-elemental spells (Aice, Alit, Afir) to significantly 
decrease the damage done by his attack spells.  You should also use Fast on your 
fighters so they can inflict more damage on Lich.  Your Mages should never 
attack because they will only do 1 damage.

evidence.quote:

from the ground.  This indicates that an Orb has regained its power.  If you 
check the menu screen, you'll see that your bottom-right Orb shines once again.  
Three more to go!  Touch the teleporter and you will be transported to the cave 
entrance.
