facts.subject: Floater
facts.text: Using the Floater from the Item screen in the middle of the Ryukhan Desert raises the Airship.

evidence.quote: Why, he must mean the Ryukhan Desert, south of Crescent Lake.  So go there, walk into the middle of the desert, say "Abracadabra" (no, just kidding), and use the Floater on your Item screen.  Ta-daah!  The Airship rises!

facts.subject: Airship
facts.text: The Airship can only land on grass or plains terrain.

evidence.quote: There's just one catch to using the Airship, and that is it can only land on grass or plains.

facts.subject: Proring
facts.text: Prorings cost 20000 gold each in Gaia and protect characters against all instant death spells.

evidence.quote:
Armor Shop:
[Gold Bracelet    50000 GP]
[ProRing          20000 GP]

What you do is, after
you get the airship, you go to the town of Gaia and buy Prorings for your
characters. These protect against ALL instant death spells.(beware though,
they cost 20,000 each.

facts.subject: Eye
facts.text: Defeating the Eye in the Ice Cave, who has 162 HP, awards 3225 exp and 3225 g.

evidence.quote:
He has 
only 162 HP, so one or two slashes from your fighter should take care of him by 
now, and killing him will net you 3225 exp and 3225 g.

facts.subject: Bahamut
facts.text: Bahamut asks for proof of courage from the Castle of Ordeal to grant honor due true warriors.

evidence.quote:
One of the caves is a long hallway which leads 
to the King of Dragons, Bahamut.  He tells you that if you can return to him 
with proof of your courage, he will grant you the honor due true warriors.  
Another dragon tells you that the test of courage takes place in the Castle of 
Ordeal to the northeast, where proof of courage can be found.

facts.subject: Airship landing
facts.text: To reach the Castle of Ordeal, land the Airship in a grass field far to the east and hike across desert, forest, and swamp.

evidence.quote:
Far to the east, there's a grass field.  You have to land there and 
then trudge through desert, forest, and swamp to reach the Castle.

facts.subject: Royal throne
facts.text: Carrying the Crown and stepping on the royal throne in the northwest corner of the 1st floor transports the party to the 2nd floor.

evidence.quote:
1st floor - The sage in the center tells you that you need the Crown to test 
your courage.  Well, you have that.  He says to take it to the royal throne, and 
bring back proof of your courage.  In the northwest corner is the royal throne.  
When you step on it, you get transported to the 2nd floor.

facts.subject: Teleport poles
facts.text: On the 2nd floor, the pole teleport sequence is: pole 1, pole 2, bottom pole 3, pole 4, bottom pole 5, pole 6, right pole 7 for Zeus Gauntlet, then bottom-most pole 8 to the stairs.

evidence.quote:
Exit the room 
you're in and touch the pole (1).  Touch the next pole (2).  Then choose the 
bottom pole (3).  Touch the next pole (4).  Choose the bottom pole (5).  Walk 
down the hall and touch the next pole (6).  Choose the right pole (7).  Walk 
right and enter the room to find a chest with the Zeus Gauntlet.  Then touch the 
bottom-most pole (8) to enter the room with the stairs.

facts.subject: 3rd floor northeast room
facts.text: The northeast room on the 3rd floor contains a Heal Staff.

evidence.quote: Northeast room:  Heal Staff

facts.subject: 3rd floor northwest room
facts.text: The northwest room on the 3rd floor contains Gold Bracelet, Ice Sword, and Iron Gauntlet.

evidence.quote: Northwest room:  Gold Bracelet, Ice Sword, Iron Gauntlet

facts.subject: 3rd floor southwest room
facts.text: The southwest room on the 3rd floor contains a House and 8795 gold.

evidence.quote: Southwest room:  House, 8795 gold

facts.subject: 3rd floor center room
facts.text: The center room on the 3rd floor contains the Tail, which serves as the proof of courage.

evidence.quote:
Center room:  Tail

The Tail is the proof of your courage.

facts.subject: Bahamut
facts.text: Returning the Tail to Bahamut upgrades all party members to a higher class.

evidence.quote:
Go back to Bahamut.  He rewards your courage by changing all of you to a higher 
class.

facts.subject: Lefein townspeople
facts.text: Townspeople in Lefein speak Lefeinish, an ancient language.

evidence.quote:
However, if you try to go to Lefein 
right now, you won't get anything at all out of it because all of the 
townspeople speak Lefeinish, an ancient language.

facts.subject: Party Creation
facts.text: Starting a new game requires choosing a character class for each of the four party members.

evidence.quote: When you start a new game, you have four characters for which you must choose a character class.

facts.subject: Fighter
facts.text: Fighters can equip the most powerful weapons and armor in the game and generally have the highest HP.

evidence.quote: Can use the most powerful weapons and armor in the game. IMHO, every party you send through the game should have at least one of these. They usually have the best HPs.

facts.subject: Thief
facts.text: Thieves have moderate attack power and the highest Agility ratings, but cannot use as many weapons as fighters.

evidence.quote: Thieves aren't as strong as fighters and can't use as many weapons, but they are useful in getting your party out of sticky situations. They have the best Agility ratings, and moderate attacks.

facts.subject: Black Belt
facts.text: The Black Belt possesses the strongest attack power when fighting unarmed, and equipping weapons actually weakens him later in the game.

evidence.quote: The Black Belt is *THE* fighter, with *THE* best attacks _unarmed_. Arming him actually weakens him somewhat, especially later on. They have HP ratings (usually) second only to the Fighter.

facts.subject: Red Mage
facts.text: Red Mages can cast both White and Black Magic and fight reasonably well, but cannot learn the most powerful spells.

evidence.quote: Red Mages can learn both White and Black Magic spells, and can even fight fairly well. However, a Red Mage cannot learn some of the most powerful spells.

facts.subject: White Mage
facts.text: White Mages can cast any White magic spell, but are poor physical fighters.

evidence.quote: Can use any White magic spells, a poor fighter, however.

facts.subject: Black Mage
facts.text: Black Mages can cast any Black magic spell, but have weak physical combat capabilities.

evidence.quote: Can use any Black magic spells, an even worse fighter.

facts.subject: White Mage
facts.text: White Mages do not gain any attack magic until they acquire the FADE spell.

evidence.quote: The Black Mages at least had the benefit of attack magic, something White Mages don't get, until FADE.

facts.subject: Invisible Man
facts.text: An invisible man can be encountered while exploring inside Castle Coneria.

evidence.quote: First, enter the castle. You can walk around the castle if you wish, talking to the people. (You can find an invisible man if you search around.)

facts.subject: King of Coneria
facts.text: Speaking to the King in Castle Coneria reveals that Princess Sara has been kidnapped by Garland.

evidence.quote: Or just walk straight up into the stairs, and from there to the King. Talk to him to learn the Princess has been kidnapped by some dude called Garland.

facts.subject: Fighter
facts.text: The recommended starting weapon and armor for a Fighter in Coneria are a Rapier and Chain Armor.

evidence.quote: Fighter |Rapier |Chain Armor

facts.subject: Black Belt
facts.text: The recommended initial purchase for a Black Belt in Coneria consists of Iron Nunchucks and Wooden Armor.

evidence.quote: Bl. Belt*|Iron Nchks|Wooden Armor

facts.subject: Thief
facts.text: The recommended initial equipment for a Thief in Coneria is a Rapier and Wooden Armor.

evidence.quote: Thief |Rapier |Wooden Armor

facts.subject: Red Mage
facts.text: The recommended starting equipment for a Red Mage in Coneria is a Rapier and Chain Armor.

evidence.quote: R. Mage |Rapier |Chain Armor

facts.subject: White Mage
facts.text: The recommended starting equipment for a White Mage in Coneria is an Iron Hammer and Cloth.

evidence.quote: Wh. Mage |Iron Hmmr |Cloth

facts.subject: Black Mage
facts.text: The recommended starting equipment for a Black Mage in Coneria is a Small Dagger and Cloth.

evidence.quote: Bl. Mage |Small Dgr.|Cloth

facts.subject: Black Belt
facts.text: An unarmed Black Belt calculates attack rating as 2 times level, and performs 4 hits per turn once hit rate reaches 32%.

evidence.quote: An unarmed BB's attack rating is always 2 x level, and he can do 4 hits a turn after he reaches 32% for hit % rating.

facts.subject: Magic Spells
facts.text: Starting level 1 magic spells in Coneria cost 100 GP each, including CURE, HARM, FIRE, LIT, and SLEP.

evidence.quote: CURE is a MUST, if you have a white or red mage. You should also get HARM, if you have a white mage. For black mages get FIRE and LIT, and SLEP. Of course, with spells at 100 GP a pop, you're going to run out of gold before you get all that.

facts.subject: Cap
facts.text: A Cap can be found as the first treasure chest along the clockwise outer perimeter of the Temple of Fiends.

evidence.quote: Items: Cabin, Heal Potion, Cap, Were Sword, Soft Potion, Rune Sword

Now head north until you reach the Temple of Fiends (the ruins). Wander around the perimeter clockwise. You should find three treasures in this order: a Cap (equip to whoever has the lowest Absorb rating; check your Status screen), a Cabin and a Heal potion.

facts.subject: Cabin
facts.text: A Cabin is found as the second chest when circling the perimeter of the Temple of Fiends clockwise.

evidence.quote: Items: Cabin, Heal Potion, Cap, Were Sword, Soft Potion, Rune Sword
Wander around the perimeter clockwise. You should find three treasures in this order: a Cap (equip to whoever has the lowest Absorb rating; check your Status screen), a Cabin and a Heal potion.

facts.subject: Heal Potion
facts.text: A Heal potion is found as the third chest along the clockwise perimeter of the Temple of Fiends.

evidence.quote: Items: Cabin, Heal Potion, Cap, Were Sword, Soft Potion, Rune Sword
Wander around the perimeter clockwise. You should find three treasures in this order: a Cap (equip to whoever has the lowest Absorb rating; check your Status screen), a Cabin and a Heal potion.

facts.subject: Garland
facts.text: Garland is confronted by heading straight through the central door of the Temple of Fiends, where he is vulnerable to the FIRE spell.

evidence.quote: Your fighting types should just pound away on him.  The White Mage should act as the healer, utilizing the Cure Spell.  The Black Mage should not fight, but instead use Fire or Lit on Garland.

Then head back to the Temple, but this time head straight up through the door. Talk to Garland, who will fling a few insults your way and then attack... Black or Red mages should flame the sucker (with the FIRE spell, not with E-Mail)

facts.subject: Princess Sara
facts.text: After rescuing Princess Sara from Garland and returning to Castle Coneria, talking to the Princess rewards the party with the Lute.

evidence.quote: After beating Garland, talk to the princess. You'll be teleported back to the castle. Talk to the king and to the princess, and the princess will give you the Lute.

facts.subject: King of Coneria
facts.text: Following Garland's defeat, the King of Coneria expresses his gratitude by ordering a bridge built to the mainland.

evidence.quote: The King will show his gratitude by ordering a bridge built to the mainland. Rest at the Inn, and then head for the bridge.

facts.subject: Matoya's Cave
facts.text: Exploring Matoya's Cave north of the Coneria bridge yields two Heal potions and a Pure potion.

evidence.quote:
three treasure Chests (one Pure Potion, two
Heal Potions), and a witch named Matoya.
Items: Heal Potion x2, Pure Potion
Cross the bridge and head north until you find a cave. Enter the cave and explore. You will find two heal potions, a pure potion, a bunch of talking brooms that say, "TCELES B HSUP."

facts.subject: Matoya
facts.text: Matoya the Witch resides in her cave having lost her Crystal, which formerly granted her sight.

evidence.quote: She will tell you that she has been blinded because someone has stolen her Crystal.
You'll also find Matoya the Witch, who seems to have lost her Crystal, which allowed her to see. You can't do much for her now, however.

facts.subject: World Map
facts.text: Holding down the B button and pressing SELECT displays the world map with the party's current location and destination points.

evidence.quote: In case you didn't figure out the broom's clue, when you leave the cave, hold down B on the controller and push SELECT. This will bring up a world map, showing your current location.

facts.subject: Pirates
facts.text: In Pravoka, talking to the pirate captain on the west side of town triggers a battle against a crew of nine pirates.

evidence.quote: Stay at the inn, and then talk to the head pirate on the west side of town. He'll order his crew of nine to attack!

facts.subject: Pirates
facts.text: Defeating the nine pirates in Pravoka awards 360 GP and a ship docked just outside the town.

evidence.quote: Winning nets you 360 GP and a ship. It's waiting for you in the dock just outside of town, but don't leave just yet.

facts.subject: Pravoka Weapons
facts.text: Pravoka sells Gloves, Wooden Shields, Scimitars, Iron Armor, and either a Short Sword or Hand Axe for 550 GP.

evidence.quote: First, buy everyone a pair of gloves. Then buy fighters a wooden shield... buy a Scimitar if you have any thieves, and either a Short Sword or a Hand Axe for fighters. They both cost the same (550 GP)... Also pick up some iron armor.

facts.subject: Pravoka Magic
facts.text: Pravoka sells the Black magic spells ICE and SLOW, and the White magic spells MUTE, ALIT, and INVS.

evidence.quote: As for magic, be sure to pick up ICE and SLOW (black), and MUTE, ALIT, and INVS (white). Red Mages should pick up at least ICE and MUTE.

facts.subject: Peninsula of Power
facts.text: Heading east into the mountains from Pravoka and continuing to the northernmost tip of the two-block-wide peninsula encounters high-level monsters like FrWOLFs, GIANTs, and TYROs due to a programming quirk.

evidence.quote: If you're really feeling lucky, then leave the town, head east into the mountains, then as far north as you can go. Due to a bug in the game, the top part of this (two-block wide) peninsula contains FrWOLFs, GIANTs, TYROs, and other relatively stronger enemies.

facts.subject: Waterfall
facts.text: The Waterfall is located north up the river near Onrac.

evidence.quote:
travel north up the river near
Onrac. You'll eventuallly run into the Waterfall.

facts.subject: Gas Dragon
facts.text: Gas Dragons in the Waterfall have 352 HP, are weak against Ice, and possess a poison attack.

evidence.quote:
Beware the Gas
Dragons, 352 HP, weak vs. Ice, and has a nasty Poison attack.

facts.subject: Robot
facts.text: Talking to the robot in the Waterfall's treasure room yields the CUBE, which grants access to the Floating Castle.

evidence.quote:
The only treasure room has a robot, and six treasures. Talk to the robot,
and he'll give you a CUBE, and tell you to use it to gain access to the
Floating Castle.

facts.subject: Treasure room
facts.text: The treasure room in the Waterfall contains a Ribbon.

evidence.quote: The treasures include another Ribbon (equip it on someone else, fast!),

facts.subject: Treasure room
facts.text: The treasure room in the Waterfall contains a Wizard Staff, which casts CONF when used in battle.

evidence.quote:
a
Wizard Staff (casts CONF when used in battle, I'd sell it.),

facts.subject: Treasure room
facts.text: The treasure room in the Waterfall contains a Defense sword, which casts RUSE when used in battle.

evidence.quote:
and a Defense
sword (casts RUSE when used in battle. It's also a good weapon for a second
Knight, Ninja, or Red Wizard.).

facts.subject: Dr. Unne
facts.text: Giving the SLAB to Dr. Unne in Melmond teaches the party the language of Lefein.

evidence.quote:
head back to Melmond. Remember Dr. Unne?
Well, find him and give him the SLAB. He'll teach you the language of Lefein.

facts.subject: Lefein citizen
facts.text: Speaking to the people in Lefein will yield the CHIME, the key to the Mirage Tower.

evidence.quote:
After a long walk south to Lefein, and talk to
the people. They'll tell you of the Floating Castle, the Sky Warriors, and of
Tiamat. One will give you the CHIME, which is the key to the Mirage Tower.

facts.subject: Secret White Magic Shop
facts.text: A secret magic shop through a break in the western wall of Lefein sells the Level 8 White Magic spell LIF2.

evidence.quote:
A break in the western wall leads to two secret magic shops. They have only
one spell each: the Level 8 White Magic spell of LIF2 (buy it, if you have a
White Wizard),

facts.subject: Secret Black Magic Shop
facts.text: A secret magic shop through a break in the western wall of Lefein sells the Level 8 Black Magic spell NUKE.

evidence.quote:
and the Level 8 Black Magic spell of NUKE (buy it, if you have
a Black Wizard).

facts.subject: Mirage Tower
facts.text: The Mirage Tower is located in the desert encircled by a mountain range.

evidence.quote:
find a place to land your airship inside the mountain range
that encircles a huge desert. You'll find the Mirage Tower in the middle of
the desert

facts.subject: Treasure room
facts.text: Floor 1 of Mirage Tower contains the Aegis Shield, which is resistant to poison.

evidence.quote:
MT Floor 1: Simple. The Treasure room here contains the Aegis Shield (equip
on your Knight, resistant to poison),

facts.subject: Treasure room
facts.text: Floor 1 of Mirage Tower contains a Heal Helmet, which casts HEAL when used during battle.

evidence.quote:
and a Heal Helmet (casts HEAL when used
during battle.)

facts.subject: Treasure room
facts.text: Floor 2 of Mirage Tower contains Thor's Hammer, which casts LIT2 in battle.

evidence.quote:
MT Floor 2: A bit more elaborate, but just circle counterclockwise. The
treasure room contains Thor's Hammer (equip on White Wizard if you've got one,
otherwise, keep it. Casts LIT2 in battle),

facts.subject: Treasure room
facts.text: Floor 2 of Mirage Tower contains the Sun Sword.

evidence.quote:
Sun Sword (a bit better than
Defense for a second Knight, Ninja, or Red Wizard),

facts.subject: Treasure room
facts.text: Floor 2 of Mirage Tower contains the Dragon Armor.

evidence.quote:
and Dragon Armor
(just as good as Opal, but without the resistance to Lightning. Good for a
second Knight only.)

facts.subject: Blue Dragon
facts.text: The Blue Dragon on Floor 3 of Mirage Tower has 454 HP, is weak against Fire, and uses a THUNDER attack.

evidence.quote:
MT Floor 3: Straightfoward. Circle around, enter the room, battle a Blue
Dragon the minute you do (454 HP, weak vs. Fire, has a THUNDER attack).

facts.subject: Transporter
facts.text: Having the CUBE allows the party to use the transporter on Floor 3 of Mirage Tower to enter the Floating Castle.

evidence.quote:
If you
have the CUBE you can use the transporter to enter the Floating Castle.

facts.subject: South branch
facts.text: The down branch on Floor 1 of Floating Castle contains the Bane Sword, which casts BANE when used in battle.

evidence.quote:
FC Floor 1: You start in the center, and you've got four branches. The top
one leads to Floor 2, left leads to GP, down leads to the Bane Sword (casts
BANE when used in battle, keep if you wish),

facts.subject: Right branch
facts.text: The right branch on Floor 1 of Floating Castle contains another Heal Helmet, a ProRing, and some GP.

evidence.quote:
right leads to another Heal
Helmet, a ProRing, and some GP.

facts.subject: Southwest branch
facts.text: The southwest branch on Floor 2 of Floating Castle leads to ADAMANT, which can be given to the Dwarven Blacksmith to forge Xcalber.

evidence.quote:
FC Floor 2: You've got 8 branches this time, and you start at the top.
Southwest leads to ADAMANT (EXIT now and go to the Dwarven Blacksmith to get
Xcalber, the second most powerful sword in the game, usable only by a Knight.)

facts.subject: Southwest branch
facts.text: Floor 2 of Floating Castle contains the Black Shirt, which casts ICE2 when used in battle.

evidence.quote:
southwest leads to the Black Shirt (casts ICE2 when
used in battle),

facts.subject: Southwest branch
facts.text: Floor 2 of Floating Castle contains the White Shirt, which casts INV2 when used in battle.

evidence.quote: and the White Shirt (casts INV2 when used in battle.).

facts.subject: West branch
facts.text: The west branch on Floor 2 of Floating Castle contains a Ribbon and an Opal Shield.

evidence.quote: West leads to another Ribbon and another Opal Shield.

facts.subject: East branch
facts.text: Heading right on Floor 3 of Floating Castle leads to a treasure room with the ProCape.

evidence.quote:
Head right for a treasure room. One of the
treasures here is the ProCape. It's basically works like the ProRing, but it
counts as a shield, and a halfway decent one at that.

facts.subject: West branch
facts.text: The west branch on Floor 3 of Floating Castle leads to a treasure room containing a Katana and the way to Floor 4.

evidence.quote:
The West
branch leads to a treasure room with a Katana (Best sword for a Ninja) and to
Floor 4

facts.subject: Floor 4 path
facts.text: On Floor 4 of Floating Castle, taking any cardinal direction and turning down the second intersection leads to a teleporter.

evidence.quote:
FC Floor 4: There are some powerful enemies here. Walk left and take the
second intersection up until you reach a teleporter. Or walk down and take the
second intersection right until you reach a teleporter. Or, walk right and
take the second intersection down until you reach a teleporter.

facts.subject: WarMech
facts.text: WarMech on Floor 5 has 1000 HP, hits physically for up to 256 damage, uses NUCLEAR for up to 400 damage to all, and awards 32000 XP and GP.

evidence.quote:
the WarMech (1000 HP, has no
strengths or weaknesses, but can do up to 256 damage to one character with
a physical attack, and his NUCLEAR blast can do up to 400 damage to all
characters. If you can manage to defeat him (FAST, NUKE, FADE, some timely
CUR4, and some good physical attacks), you are very well rewarded: 32000 XP
and GP.

facts.subject: Tiamat
facts.text: Tiamat has 1000 HP, resists elementals, and is weak against BRAK and BANE attacks like the Bane Sword.

evidence.quote:
Tiamat, the Fiend of Wind, is the toughest of the Fiends. 1000 HP, and
strong against elementals. (Both NP and Ben Siron's guides claim that he is
also weak against BRAK and BANE. If you've got somebody with a Bane Sword that
isn't really helping the cause much, the go ahead and try, it does
occasionally work, but don't waste any spell charges on it.)

facts.subject: Black Orb
facts.text: Talking to Garland's Black Orb in the Temple of Fiends teleports the party 2000 years into the past.

evidence.quote: Head to the black orb and then you will be transported 2000 years back into

When you're through
messing around, talk to Garland's Black Orb, and you'll be teleported to the
Temple of Fiends, 2000 years ago.

facts.subject: Frost Dragon
facts.text: Frost Dragons on Floor 1 of the Temple of Fiends appear in groups of 3 or 4 and use Frost.

evidence.quote:
Watch out for
the Frost Dragons, they come 3 or 4 at a time and will Frost you to death if
you're not careful.

facts.subject: Phantom
facts.text: Entering the central room on Floor 3 triggers a battle against the Phantom, who is undead.

evidence.quote:
Floor 3: Head for the central room. When you enter you'll fight the Phantom,
who's easily dispatched (he's undead, if that helps).

If 
you're too insecure to fight, he's undead, so FIR3 or HRM3,4 will do nicely.

facts.subject: Treasure chests
facts.text: The two treasure chests on Floor 3 contain 45000 and 65000 GP.

evidence.quote:
The two treasure chests
are worth 45000 and 65000 GP.

facts.subject: Stone plate
facts.text: The Stone plate on Floor 3 of the Temple of Fiends requires the LUTE to pass.

evidence.quote:
Another Stone plate is here, but remember the
LUTE you've been carrying from the beginning?

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Lich guards the stairs on Basement 1 and is capable of casting NUKE.

evidence.quote:
Right before the stairs you'll run into your good pal Lich, the Earth Fiend.
Same tactics generally work, except he can use NUKE now.

facts.subject: Basement 2
facts.text: Another ProCape can be found by exploring Basement 2 of the Temple of Fiends.

evidence.quote:
Basement 2: This floor contains enemies from the Gurgu Volcano, just in
greater quantity. You can find another ProCape on this level, if you take the
time to explore.

facts.subject: Kary
facts.text: Kary is fought again near the exit stairs on Basement 2 of the Temple of Fiends.

evidence.quote:
Travel
to the right then take the exit and head south then left to the stairs to get
out. You'll fight Kary again before you leave.

facts.subject: Kraken
facts.text: Kraken is fought again on the way out of Basement 3 of the Temple of Fiends.

evidence.quote:
Basement 3: This floor contains enemies from the Sea Shrine, just in greater
quantity. Make your way south, and take out Kraken again on the way out.

facts.subject: Southeastern room
facts.text: A small room off the southeastern tail on Basement 4 contains the Masmune.

evidence.quote:
It's divided into four squares, with the southeastern one having a
'tail' which has a small room with the Masmune.

facts.subject: Tiamat
facts.text: Tiamat is fought in the northeastern square on Basement 4 of the Temple of Fiends.

evidence.quote:
When you've got it, head for the Northeastern square,
and say 'hola' (or 'adios' if you prefer) to Tiamat on the way down.

facts.subject: Chaos
facts.text: Chaos has 2000 HP, casts CUR4 as his fourth spell, and uses Crack, Inferno for up to 384 Fire damage, and Swirl for up to 256 physical damage.

evidence.quote:
At any rate, he has 2000 HP, resistance to everything, some killer magic
(including an annoying CUR4 which is his fourth regular spell he uses), some
killer attacks (Crack - Instant death to all warriors [ProRing, anyone?],
Inferno - Up to 384 points of Fire damage to all warriors [Ribbon or WALL],
Swirl - Up to 256 physical damage to all warriors... you get the idea.)

facts.subject: Chaos
facts.text: Nintendo Power recommends being at least Level 27 to fight Chaos, while the author recommends Level 35.

evidence.quote:
But if you're at at least 
level 27 or so, you have a good chance of winning.
NP recommends you be at least Level 27 to fight him. I recommend about 35.

facts.subject: Sliding puzzle
facts.text: Pressing A and B together 55 times while inside the sailing ship opens a sliding puzzle minigame.

evidence.quote:
get in
the sailing ship, press A and B together 55 times to play a sliding puzzle
game.

facts.subject: Dragon Armour
facts.text: Dragon Armour is reported to make its wearer resistant to Fire, Ice, and Lightning.

evidence.quote:
Dave Connoy reports that the Dragon Armour makes its wearer resistant to
Fire/Ice/Lightning.

facts.subject: ARUB
facts.text: ARUB displays a resist magic message and is reported to grant resistance to all magic.

evidence.quote:
Somebody reported that ARUB granted resistance to all magic, not just
instant-death spells. This was based on the fact that a "resist magic" message
pops up when you use it.

facts.subject: Sliding Puzzle
facts.text: Pushing A and B together 55 times while sailing unlocks a sliding puzzle game.

evidence.quote: push A and B together 55 times to play a sliding puzzle game.

facts.subject: Aldi Sea Port
facts.text: Sailing due south of Coneria and then west into a port leads to a short walk from Elfland and the Castle of Elf.

evidence.quote: head due south of Coneria, and then west into a port. This lets you off a short walk's distance from Elfland and the Castle of Elf.

facts.subject: Prince of the Elves
facts.text: The Prince of the Elves is under a sleeping spell cast by Astos that can only be broken with an Herb.

evidence.quote: Here you'll find that the Prince of the Elves is under a sleeping spell cast on him by Astos, the dark elf. You'll also hear that only a Herb will wake him up.

facts.subject: Matoya
facts.text: Matoya possesses the herb required to awaken the sleeping elf prince.

evidence.quote: You'll also hear that Matoya has such an herb.

facts.subject: Elfland Weapon and Armor Shops
facts.text: Fighters can buy a Silver Sword, an Iron Shield, and a Wooden Helmet in Elfland.

evidence.quote: Buy Fighters a Silver sword, an Iron shield, and a Wooden helmet.

facts.subject: Level 3 Magic
facts.text: Level 3 magic spells available in Elfland include CUR2, FIR2, LIT2, HRM2, and AFIR.

evidence.quote: As far as spells go, CUR2, FIR2, and LIT2 are musts for level 3 magic. If you have a White Mage, buy HRM2 as well. AFIR is useful as well.

facts.subject: Level 4 Magic
facts.text: Level 4 magic spells available in Elfland include PURE, FAST, and ICE2.

evidence.quote: For level 4 magic, buy PURE, FAST, and ICE2 for sure, and then just buy whatever floats your boat, if you want to come up with the cash.

facts.subject: King
facts.text: A lone King inside the deserted Northwest Castle claims that Astos stole his crown.

evidence.quote: Enter and you'll find a deserted castle filled with bats, some more of those famous locked doors, and a lone King, who claims that Astos has stolen his crown.

facts.subject: Marsh Cave North Path
facts.text: Taking the north path at the entrance of the Marsh Cave leads to a room with treasure chests.

evidence.quote: When you first enter the Marsh Cave, you'll have the option to go north or south. The north path leads to a room with a few treasure chests, with nothing of value.

facts.subject: Marsh Cave South Path
facts.text: Taking the south path in the Marsh Cave leads down stairs to another room with stairs to the third basement.

evidence.quote: Head south, take the stairs to another room. Make your way to the little room at the bottom, where more stairs await.

facts.subject: Wizards
facts.text: In the third basement of the Marsh Cave, entering the room third from the top and second from the left triggers a fight with Wizards.

evidence.quote: Here in the third basement, you'll find a four by four arrangement of little rooms...go into the room third from the top, and second from the left. You'll have to fight a group of Wizards.

facts.subject: Wizards
facts.text: Wizards possess 84 hit points, are weak against LIT, and guard the crown.

evidence.quote: Wizards have 84 hit points, and a weakness for LIT (you did buy LIT2 before you came here, didn't you?). After defeating them take the crown and run.

facts.subject: Astos
facts.text: Speaking to the King in the Northwest Castle reveals he is Astos, initiating a battle.

evidence.quote: Talk to the King again and he will reveal that he is really Astos, the SOB that stole Matoya's crystal and casted the sleeping spell on the prince. You're gonna have to fight him.

facts.subject: Astos
facts.text: Astos has 168 HP, casts RUB, and yields Matoya's Crystal upon defeat.

evidence.quote: After the battle you will have recieved the Crystal from Astos.

Astos has 168 HP and an attitude to boot. Keep nailing him with your strongest attacks and magic, healing if necessary (or if possible. This dude knows RUB!) When (or if) you win, you'll get Matoya's CRYSTAL.

facts.subject: Matoya
facts.text: Returning the Crystal to Matoya in her cave earns the Herb in exchange.

evidence.quote: Return to her cave, give her the CRYSTAL in exchange for the HERB.

facts.subject: Mystic Key
facts.text: Giving the Herb to the Prince in the Castle of Elves awakens him and rewards the party with the Mystic Key.

evidence.quote: Go back to the Castle of Elves, give the Prince the HERB. When he wakes up, he'll give your party the Mystic KEY, which will open up all those blasted locked doors.

facts.subject: Locked Room
facts.text: Unlocking the doors in Castle Coneria provides TNT.

evidence.quote: definitely unlock the doors in Castle Coneria, for some TNT.

facts.subject: Coneria Port
facts.text: Sailing west from the port of Coneria to the next port brings the party near the Dwarven Cave.

evidence.quote: head west from the port of Coneria, to the next port you find. This will put you a short way away from the Dwarven Cave.

facts.subject: Dwarven Cave
facts.text: Treasures found in the Dwarven Cave include an Iron Helmet and Silver Armor.

evidence.quote: The Iron Helmet is worth keeping if you've got a Fighter, but sell everything else. The Silver Armor is much more expensive than Iron, but it's also a lot weaker.

facts.subject: Dwarven Cave
facts.text: The Dragon Sword is found in the Dwarven Cave.

evidence.quote: The Dragon Sword might be good for thieves, but contrary to popular belief, FF1 weapons have no racial modifers.

facts.subject: Nerrick
facts.text: Delivering TNT to Nerrick in the Dwarven Cave allows him to complete the canal between the Aldi Sea and the Western Sea.

evidence.quote:
There isn't a lot to be done here, other than go on a massive looting
raid on the treasure room, and to give your TNT to a dwarf named
Nerrick who will use it to make a Canal just south of the cave, which
will allow you passage to Melmond and other lands to the west of the
area in which you were limited too.

You'll eventually find Nerrick, who is trying to make a canal between the Aldi Sea and the Western Sea. He's short on TNT at the moment, so if you're nice enough to lend him some (like you really have a choice), he can complete the job and you can move on.

facts.subject: Canal
facts.text: Sailing through the newly opened canal allows the ship to dock next to Melmond.

evidence.quote: Sail your ship through the newly formed canal, and dock up next to Melmond.

facts.subject: Melmond Armor Shop
facts.text: The armor shop in Melmond sells Steel Armor for 45000 GP.

evidence.quote: The armor shop has Steel Armor, one of the best in the game for Fighters. However, it comes with a 45000 GP price tag.

facts.subject: Undead
facts.text: Walking in front of the three treasure chests behind the locked door in the Northwest Castle triggers attacks by Undead creatures.

evidence.quote: The Locked Door of the Northwest Castle is one such place. The three treasure chests contain nothing of use (sell them!), but walking in front of them always triggers an attack by Undead creatures.

facts.subject: Melmond Shops
facts.text: Silver Bracelets and Iron Gauntlets can be purchased in Melmond.

evidence.quote: After getting some money, buy Silver Bracelets for your black or white mages, if any, and some Iron Gauntlets for fighters.

facts.subject: Level 5 Magic
facts.text: Spells discussed for acquisition in Melmond include CUR3, FIR3, LIFE, HRM3, and WARP.

evidence.quote: Namely let's talk CUR3, FIR3. If you have a White Mage, do get LIFE and HRM3 as well. If you have a Red or Black Mage, leave a spot for WARP.

facts.subject: Melmond
facts.text: Heading south past the rotting earth from Melmond leads to the Earth Cave.

evidence.quote: leave Melmond and head south past the rotting earth to the Earth Cave.

facts.subject: Hall of Giants
facts.text: The western hall of Basement 1 in the Earth Cave is known as The Hall of Giants and contains Giants and Iguanas.

evidence.quote: Basement 1: Be warned of the western hall when you enter the cave. Known as "The Hall of Giants", It contains nothing but Giants and Iguanas.

facts.subject: Earth Elemental
facts.text: Stepping in front of most chests in the treasure rooms of Basement 1 triggers a fight with an Earth elemental, which is weak against FIRE.

evidence.quote: enter any of the three treasure rooms and step in front of a chest. Most of the chests have an automatic fight with an Earth elemental, which has a weakness against FIRE

facts.subject: Basement 1 Stairs
facts.text: Heading east from the stairs in Basement 1 descends to Basement 2, where navigating right and down leads through the floor.

evidence.quote: So, head east from the stairs, and descend a level....Basement 2: This basement is made of several connecting chambers. Generally head to the right and down, and you should make your way through.

facts.subject: Vampire
facts.text: Heading clockwise through Basement 3 leads to the Vampire, who has 156 HP, is weak to FIRE and HARM, and yields the Ruby.

evidence.quote: In the center room is a Vampire, which you will have to defeat for the Ruby....however you attain the Ruby.
Work your way through the Earth Cave, and defeat the...Vampire which is deep inside. Once you have the Ruby, head out of the

Basement 3: This basement is pretty simple, too. Just try to head clockwise through the level until you meet the Vampire....The Vampire is pretty easy. He has 156 HP, and weaknesses against FIRE and HARM....You'll win a RUBY for your troubles.

facts.subject: Stone Plate
facts.text: Exploration beyond the Vampire in the Earth Cave is halted by a stone plate.

evidence.quote: You can try to continue, if you like, but you'll soon be stopped by a stone plate.

facts.subject: Titan
facts.text: Entering the Titan's Tunnel to the southwest and feeding the Ruby to the Titan allows the party to pass through.

evidence.quote: You'll enter the Titan's Tunnel. Feed the Titan the RUBY, and he'll let you pass through.

facts.subject: Titan's Tunnel
facts.text: Treasure chests in the Titan's Tunnel contain a Great Axe and a Silver Helmet.

evidence.quote: The treasure chests in the cave contain a Great Axe and a Silver Helmet for your fighter.

facts.subject: Sarda
facts.text: In Sarda's Cave south of the Titan's Tunnel exit, Sarda gives the party the Rod to use on the stone plate.

evidence.quote: At the other exit of the Tunnel, head south to Sarda's Cave. He'll give you the ROD and tell you to use it on the stone plate to find the source of the earth's rot.

facts.subject: Stone Plate
facts.text: Using the Rod on the stone plate in the Earth Cave allows the party to continue downward.

evidence.quote: Head back to the stone plate, use the ROD, and continue downward.

facts.subject: Basement 4
facts.text: Basement 4 of the Earth Cave contains stone-inflicting Cockatrices and a Silver Shield.

evidence.quote: Basement 4: The Fourth basement has the same interconnecting chambers of the past two levels. Be careful of the Cockatrices here; they have a habit getting your characters stoned. Just keep heading left. Also there's a Silver Shield to be found here.

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Talking to the orb in Basement 5 triggers a battle with Lich, who has 400 HP and is weak against FIRE and HARM.

evidence.quote: Fire is your best bet to winning this match. Use fire spells from your mages and have the other party members attack as normal.

Monster:    | Lich
HP:         | 400
Attack Avg: | 40-80
Attack Eff. | NA
EXP:        | 2200
Gold:       | 3000
Class:      | Undead
Weaknesses: | Fire
Attacks:    | Ice2, Slp2, Fast, Lit2, Hold, Fir2, Slow, Slep
Strong vs.: | Ice, Rub, Bane, Stun, Slep, Brak
Location:   | Earth Cave

enter the room and talk to the orb. It will shatter, leaving you to do battle with Lich, the Fiend of the Earth....Here are his vitals: 400 HP, weak against FIRE, and HARM type spells do a good bit of damage as well.

facts.subject: Throne
facts.text: Stepping onto the throne behind Lich warps the party out of the Earth Cave and restores light to one of the Orbs.

evidence.quote: If you defeat Lich, step foward onto the throne, which will automatically warp you out of the cave. Check out your subscreen when you leave: one of your ORBS will have regained it's light.

facts.subject: Crescent Lake Equipment Shops
facts.text: Sailing east past Elfland leads to Crescent Lake, where shops sell Silver equipment including the Silver Axe and Silver Armor.

evidence.quote: Follow the shore to a dock to the northeast of Crescent Lake (noted chiefly for its proximity to a crecent-shaped lake). In this town, you'll find some Silver equipment, buy some, but avoid that Silver Armor like the rot of the earth. The Silver Axe is good for your fighter.

facts.subject: Level 6 Magic
facts.text: Magic spells sold in Crescent Lake include SOFT, INV2, EXIT, and LIT3.

evidence.quote: Buy SOFT if you have a white mage. Buy INV2 now if you have a white mage, later if you have a Red mage...Leave a slot for EXIT, be your white magic user White or Red...For a black mage get LIT3

facts.subject: Circle of Sages
facts.text: Speaking to the Circle of Sages in Crescent Lake rewards the party with the Canoe, enabling travel along rivers.

evidence.quote: explore the city until you find the Circle of Sages. Talk to each one of them. One of them will give you a CANOE, which will allow you to row your way through rivers.

facts.subject: River
facts.text: Traveling along the river by canoe leads to the Gurgu Volcano.

evidence.quote: crank up your CANOE and explore the river. Watch out for the river monsters. Eventually you'll find yourself at the Gurgu Volcano.

facts.subject: Lava
facts.text: Walking across lava in Basement 1 of the Gurgu Volcano damages the party with every step.

evidence.quote: Basement 1: The first basement of the volcano is not difficult to navigate. Just beware that the lava does damage to you at every step, but you can't avoid it.

facts.subject: Basement 2 Treasure Room
facts.text: The treasure room in Basement 2 of the Gurgu Volcano contains 3 Silver Helmets, a Silver Shield, a Silver Axe, potions, and gold.

evidence.quote: Basement 2: The second basement is really easy: just head straight to the left. You can explore the treasure room if you wish, 3 Silver Helmets, a silver shield, a silver axe, some potions, and a bit of gold will be your reward.

facts.subject: Fire Elementals
facts.text: Fire elementals guard most of the treasure chests in Basement 2 of the Gurgu Volcano.

evidence.quote: Just watch out for the Fire elementals that guard most of the treasure.

facts.subject: Basement 3A Stairs
facts.text: In Basement 3A of the Gurgu Volcano, heading right until reaching the end leads to stairs.

evidence.quote: Basement 3A: This level is easy too. Head Right until you can't no more, then take the stairs.

facts.subject: Basement 4A Stairs
facts.text: Basement 4A of the Gurgu Volcano is filled with lava and contains stairs leading up to Basement 3B.

evidence.quote: Basement 4A: This floor presents no mazes, just completely filled with lava. The stairs will take you up to Basement 3B.

facts.subject: Basement 3B Path
facts.text: Navigating Basement 3B in the Gurgu Volcano requires walking down, taking the first left, heading down again, and moving all the way left.

evidence.quote: Basement 3B: Walk down, take the first left, then down again, then all the way left.

facts.subject: Northwest Treasure Room
facts.text: The northwest treasure room of Basement 4B contains the Ice Sword and a Flame Shield.

evidence.quote: Basement 4B: This level is filled with treasure rooms. The one in the northwest corner contains the Ice Sword, which should be equipped on your Fighter (or Red Mage, if you wish). It also has a Flame Shield, which is good against Ice attacks

facts.subject: West Branch
facts.text: In Basement 5 of the Gurgu Volcano, the west branch of the 8 branches leads to the Flame Armor.

evidence.quote: Basement 5: This room is simple. It has 8 branches. The west branch leads to the Flame Armor (good against Ice attacks), and the southwest branch leads to Kary, the fiend of Fire.

facts.subject: Kary
facts.text: The southwest branch of Basement 5 leads to Kary, who has 600 HP and is resistant to all elements.

evidence.quote: Kary has 600 HP, and is resistant to all Elementals.

facts.subject: Throne
facts.text: Stepping onto the throne after defeating Kary exits the Gurgu Volcano and lights another Orb.

evidence.quote: After victory, step on the throne to exit the Volcano. You'll see that yet another ORB has lighted.

facts.subject: Ice Cave
facts.text: The Ice Cave is reached by taking the ship north from Crescent Lake, docking at a river mouth, and exploring the rivers by canoe.

evidence.quote: When you're done there, take your ship and follow the coastline to the north. Dock your ship at the mouth of a river, and take the CANOE for a spin. Explore these rivers until you reach the Ice Cave.

facts.subject: Basement 1
facts.text: From Basement 1, head right, down, left, and take the stairs to reach Basement 2A.

evidence.quote: Basement 1: Head right, head down, head left, take stairs.

facts.subject: Basement 2A
facts.text: From Basement 2A, take either left then down, or down then left, and take the stairs.

evidence.quote: Basement 2A: Either Left then down, or down then left. Take Stairs.

facts.subject: Treasure room
facts.text: A Flame Sword can be collected inside the treasure room on Basement 2B.

evidence.quote: Basement 2B: Circle around and enter the treasure room. You'll be able to get to the Flame Sword (useless, unless you have a second Fighter or Red Mage), and a Cloth (completely worthless!).

facts.subject: Treasure room
facts.text: A Cloth can be found inside the treasure room on Basement 2B.

evidence.quote: Basement 2B: Circle around and enter the treasure room. You'll be able to get to the Flame Sword (useless, unless you have a second Fighter or Red Mage), and a Cloth (completely worthless!).

facts.subject: Basement 2B
facts.text: Dropping into a pitfall on Basement 2B leads down to Basement 3B.

evidence.quote: Drop into a pitfall to get to: Basement 3B: You'll end up in a little room, and the next step will always lead to a battle with a legion of Undead creatures.

facts.subject: Basement 3B
facts.text: Stairs in the southeastern corner of Basement 3B lead to the far side of Basement 1.

evidence.quote: You'll find the stairs in a southeastern corner. Basement 1 revisited: You'll end up on the far side of Basement one.

facts.subject: Basement 1 revisited
facts.text: Stepping into the pitfall in a treasure room on Basement 1 drops you to Basement 2B revisited.

evidence.quote: Explore the treasure rooms: one has a single pitfall. Step in it to get to: Basement 2B revisited: You'll be within reach of the treasure chest you couldn't get to earlier.

facts.subject: Eye
facts.text: Stepping in front of the treasure chest on Basement 2B triggers a battle against the Eye.

evidence.quote: When you step in front of it, you'll have to battle the Eye.

facts.subject: Eye
facts.text: The Eye has 162 HP, casts XXXX, BRAK, RUB, and awards 3225 EXP and 3225 GP.

evidence.quote: The Eye has 162 HP and can use XXXX, BRAK, RUB, and other instant death spells... You'll get 3225 EXP (divided among surviving characters) and 3225 GP.

facts.subject: Treasure chest
facts.text: The Floater is obtained from the treasure chest guarded by the Eye on Basement 2B.

evidence.quote: After defeating this enemy, open the Treasure Chest to find the FLOATER!
Take the treasure from the chest (the all-important FLOATER), and drop into a pitfall.

facts.subject: AIRSHIP
facts.text: Using the Floater inside the Ryukahn Desert raises the Airship.

evidence.quote: Instead, walk on land to the nearby Ryukahn* Desert. Step inside the desert and use the FLOATER to get the AIRSHIP.

facts.subject: World map
facts.text: Holding down B and pressing Select while flying in the Airship displays the world map.

evidence.quote: If you get lost flying around, hold down B and push Select to see the world map.

facts.subject: Bahamut
facts.text: Bahamut, the King of the Dragons of Cardia, is found inside a cave on the islands.

evidence.quote: You'll find caves inhabited by Dragons (friendly ones, don't worry.) In one cave you'll find Bahamut, the King of the Dragons of Cardia.

facts.subject: Castle of Ordeal
facts.text: On Floor 1 of Castle of Ordeal, enter the northwest room to proceed to Floor 2.

evidence.quote: Floor 1: No enemies, just take the northwest room to get to Floor 2.

facts.subject: Pillars
facts.text: To navigate the Floor 2 maze, take the only column, then the only pillar, take the bottom pillar, take the only column, take the bottom pillar, take the single column at the end of the south corridor, take the right pillar, head east to the treasure room, then take the leftmost corridor south and enter the leftmost pillar to reach the stairs.

evidence.quote: Head out to the only column you can reach. This will warp you to another part of the room. Again, take the only pillar. This warps you to a choice of two pillars. Take the bottom. After this warp, take the only column you can reach. This will again take you to a choice of two. Again, take the bottom. This places you in a long corridor leading south. It leads to only one column, so take it. You have again a choice of two pillars. Take the one on the right. This places you in a corridor leading east. Head east to a treasure room... Take the leftmost corridor heading south and take the leftmost pillar. This warps you to a little room with one set of stairs.

facts.subject: Treasure room
facts.text: A gold bracelet is found inside the treasure room on Floor 2 of the Castle of Ordeal.

evidence.quote: Head east to a treasure room. It contains a gold bracelet.

facts.subject: Floor 3
facts.text: An Ice sword is located among the treasures on Floor 3 of the Castle of Ordeal.

evidence.quote: Floor 3: There are no mazes or branching paths here, just some stronger enemies and some treasure, including an Ice sword

facts.subject: Floor 3
facts.text: A Heal Staff, which casts HEAL when used as an item in battle, is found on Floor 3.

evidence.quote: a Heal Staff (keep it but don't equip.. casts the spell of HEAL if used as an item in battle)

facts.subject: Floor 3
facts.text: The Zeus Gauntlet, which casts LIT2 when used in battle, is located on Floor 3.

evidence.quote: the Zeus Gauntlet (keep but don't equip, casts LIT2 if used in battle).

facts.subject: Zombie Dragons
facts.text: Zombie Dragons have 268 HP each and are weak against FIRE and HARM.

evidence.quote: Stepping in front of the chest will start a fight with Zombie Dragons (268 HP each, weak vs. FIRE and HARM as usual.)

facts.subject: Throne chest
facts.text: The Rat's Tail is obtained from the treasure chest guarded by the Zombie Dragons in front of the throne.

evidence.quote: Eventually you'll reach a throne with a treasure chest in front. Stepping in front of the chest will start a fight with Zombie Dragons... Collect the Rat's TAIL and step on the throne to warp back to floor one and exit.

facts.subject: Bahamut
facts.text: Presenting the Rat's Tail to Bahamut upgrades the classes of the party members.

evidence.quote: Collect the Rat's TAIL and step on the throne to warp back to floor one and exit. Return to Bahamut's throne and present him the TAIL. He will then upgrade your characters' class as follows:

facts.subject: Fighter
facts.text: Upgrading a Fighter turns them into a Knight, enabling them to equip the strongest weapons and armor and use low-level White Magic.

evidence.quote:
Fighter  | Knight        | Can equip all the strongest weapons and armor. Also
         |               | can use some low-level White Magic spells.

facts.subject: Thief
facts.text: Upgrading a Thief turns them into a Ninja, allowing them to use more weapons, armor, and up to Level 4 Black Magic.

evidence.quote: Instead of having one hard hitting team member, the Thief turned Ninja adds in a second choice in this area.

Thief    | Ninja         | Can now use many more weapons and armor and can use
         |               | up to Level 4 Black Magic.

facts.subject: BlackBelt
facts.text: Upgrading a BlackBelt turns them into a Master.

evidence.quote: BlackBelt| Master        | Just kicks butt as usual.

facts.subject: Red Mage
facts.text: Upgrading a Red Mage turns them into a Red Wizard, granting access to additional weapons and spells.

evidence.quote: Red Mage | Red Wizard    | Can now use some more weapons and spells.

facts.subject: WhiteMage
facts.text: Upgrading a WhiteMage turns them into a White Wizard, enabling them to use all White Magic spells.

evidence.quote: WhiteMage| White Wizard  | Can now use all White Magic Spells

facts.subject: BlackMage
facts.text: Upgrading a BlackMage turns them into a Black Wizard, enabling them to use all Black Magic spells.

evidence.quote: BlackMage| Black Wizard  | Can now use all Black Magic Spells.

facts.subject: Gaia shop
facts.text: ProRings can be purchased in the town of Gaia for 20000 GP each to provide protection against instant death attacks.

evidence.quote: But for now buy ProRings for everybody (20000GP each, ouch). They count as Gauntlets, they might not have the best absorb rating, but protection from instant death attacks (RUB, XXXX, and SQUINT) is definitely worth it!

facts.subject: Caravan
facts.text: The Caravan in the desert on the Northwestern continent sells a Bottle for 50000 GP.

evidence.quote: A little piece of desert will surrounded by forests. That's where the Caravan is, and the dude there is selling a BOTTLE for 50000GP.

facts.subject: Fairy
facts.text: Using the Bottle causes a Fairy to appear in the spring at Gaia, who gives the player the Oxyale.

evidence.quote: Buy it, and use it, and the Fairy will show up in the spring in the northeast corner of Gaia. Talk to her and you'll get the OXYALE, which you need to enter the Sea Shrine.

facts.subject: Submarine
facts.text: A submarine found in the town of Onrac leads to the Sea Shrine if the player possesses the Oxyale.

evidence.quote:
Head back to Onrac
(use your B Button + SELECT map if need be to find it), go into Onrac, buy
any supplies that you may need, and then go enter the Submarine to appear
underneath the waves.
You can pass because you have Oxyale.  Touching the submarine transports you to the Sea Shrine.
The River of the Northwestern continent leads up to the town of Onrac... but a submarine can be found here that leads to the Sea Shrine, if you've got the OXYALE.

facts.subject: Floor 3A
facts.text: Taking the right set of stairs in the top rooms of Floor 3A leads up to Floor 4A.

evidence.quote: Sea Shrine, Floor 3A: Simple level... There are two sets of stairs here, in the top two rooms. Take the ones on the right.

facts.subject: Floor 4A
facts.text: Opal Armor can be found in the treasure rooms of Floor 4A in the Sea Shrine.

evidence.quote: Floor 4A: This level is kind of loopy but not hard. Take time to visit all the treasure rooms. You'll get Opal Armor (equip on your Knight), a Light Axe (keep this: casts HRM2 if used in battle), and a Mage Staff (keep it: casts FIR2 if used in battle).

facts.subject: Floor 4A
facts.text: A Light Axe, which casts HRM2 when used in battle, is obtained on Floor 4A.

evidence.quote: Floor 4A: This level is kind of loopy but not hard. Take time to visit all the treasure rooms. You'll get Opal Armor (equip on your Knight), a Light Axe (keep this: casts HRM2 if used in battle), and a Mage Staff (keep it: casts FIR2 if used in battle).

facts.subject: Floor 4A
facts.text: A Mage Staff, which casts FIR2 when used in battle, is found in a treasure room on Floor 4A.

evidence.quote: Floor 4A: This level is kind of loopy but not hard. Take time to visit all the treasure rooms. You'll get Opal Armor (equip on your Knight), a Light Axe (keep this: casts HRM2 if used in battle), and a Mage Staff (keep it: casts FIR2 if used in battle).

facts.subject: Floor 4A
facts.text: Stairs in the southeastern corner of Floor 4A lead to Floor 5.

evidence.quote: Stairs are in the southeastern corner. Floor 5: No enemies, just mermaids and lots of treasure.

facts.subject: Treasure room
facts.text: The Slab is located in the northeastern treasure room of Floor 5, reached by walking to the northwest corner and heading left through a corridor.

evidence.quote: Walk to the Northwestern corner and head to the left through a long corridor to get to the treasure room on the northeaster corner (off one side of the screen and on to the other...). It contains the SLAB, which is very important.

facts.subject: Floor 3A revisited
facts.text: Taking the left set of stairs on Floor 3A leads to Floor 2A.

evidence.quote: Floor 3A revisited: Take the left set of stairs this time. Floor 2A: Head generally north and take the stairs.

facts.subject: Floor 2B
facts.text: A second Light Axe can be found in the treasure rooms on Floor 2B.

evidence.quote: Floor 2B: Another loopy room. Look through all the treasure rooms for another Light Axe and a Ribbon

facts.subject: Floor 2B
facts.text: A Ribbon is found on Floor 2B, functioning as a helmet that protects against ICE, FIRE, LIT, FLASH, HOLD, GLANCE, DARK, INK, STINGER, STOP, and POISON.

evidence.quote: Look through all the treasure rooms for another Light Axe and a Ribbon (Equip on somebody NOW. Counts as a helmet, very weak (absorb of 1, evade% of 1), but protects against ICE, FIRE, LIT, FLASH, HOLD, GLANCE, DARK, INK, STINGER, STOP, and POISON.

facts.subject: Kraken
facts.text: Kraken has 800 HP, is weak against LIT, and is strong against QAKE and FIRE.

evidence.quote: Kraken          800     Ink (Dark),Lit2                  Lit
Vitals: 800 HP, weak vs. LIT, and strong against QAKE and FIRE.

facts.subject: Ice Armor
facts.text: Ice armors provide protection against Fire, and Fire armors provide protection against Ice.

evidence.quote:
Ice armors provide protection against Fire, and Fire armors likewise against 
Ice.

facts.subject: Ribbon
facts.text: The Ribbon grants protection against all elements.

evidence.quote: The Ribbon also gives protection against all the elements.

facts.subject: Aegis Shield
facts.text: The Aegis Shield provides protection against poison status when it is not inflicted by a regular attack.

evidence.quote:
Also, I read 
on Ben Siron's FF1 Handbook that the Aegis Shield provides protection against 
poison status, as long as it is not inflicted with the regular attack.

facts.subject: Spiked Square
facts.text: Stepping on a spiked square in a cave or tower always triggers a battle every time.

evidence.quote:
Spiked Square-  Normally, you will encounter enemies randomly if you are in a 
cave or tower.  However, sometimes, there are special squares where you can step 
where you will always find the same battle, every time you step there.

facts.subject: Garland
facts.text: Garland has approximately 80 to 100 HP and can be countered by casting RUSE, FOG, and CURE to mitigate his damage.

evidence.quote: I have the Red and Black Mages cast Fire or Lit on him, your choice and both do about the same amount of damage.

BOSS FIGHT-Garland
HP: 80-100 or something like that
    This guy shouldn't be too hard.  He can to some heavy damage to some of your 
ill-equipped mages, but you can just cast RUSE, FOG, and CURE to help that.

facts.subject: World Map
