Earth Cave.

facts.subject: Manticore
facts.text: A Manticore can use STINGER to poison all party members.

evidence.quote: I think one is a Manticore or something like that.  He can use STINGER, which will cause all your party members to get poisoned.

facts.subject: Wizard Ogre
facts.text: A Wizard Ogre on a spiked square casts MUTE, SLOW, and RUSE, and can be countered with MUTE, FAST, LOCK, or AMUT.

evidence.quote: First, he used MUTE and he shut my mages up.  Then, he used SLOW and disabled my fighters.  Then, so the mages couldn't attack him, he kept using RUSE on himself...So, to fight him, use MUTE if you have it.  If he uses RUSE too much, use FAST on your fighters or cast LOCK on him.  You could also use AMUT to stop him from being a problem in the first place.

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Lich has 400 HP and casts FIR2 and ICE2, which can be mitigated with AFIR and AICE.

evidence.quote: HP-400 I think...Also, LICH will use FIR2 and ICE2, so make sure you use AFIR and AICE to help out a bit.

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: FIR3 will never do more than 40-50 damage against Lich.

evidence.quote: Nintendo Power says that LICH is weak against Fire, but even FIR3 will never do more than 40-50 damage, so don't bother with that.

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: SLO2 can successfully afflict Lich during the boss fight.

evidence.quote: One time, I even got SLO2 to work on LICH.  Wow, that helped immensely.

facts.subject: Circle of Sages
facts.text: Visiting the Circle of Sages in Crescent Lake grants the CANOE.

evidence.quote: Now it's time to talk go to the Circle of Sages.  They will tell you some semi-important information, but the real thing you're after is the CANOE.

facts.subject: Castle of Ordeal
facts.text: The author recommends going to the Castle of Ordeal first before Gurgu Volcano and the Ice Cave.

evidence.quote: The Castle of Ordeal is actually last in line of the plot, but I recommend going here first.

facts.subject: Medusa
facts.text: Medusas in the Castle of Ordeal travel in packs and can turn the whole party to stone in a round or two.

evidence.quote: There will be Medusas that travel in packs and can easily turn your whole party to stone in just a round or two.

facts.subject: Ice Cave
facts.text: The Ice Cave is considered the hardest cave because enemies use RUB and auto-kill attacks while the party lacks a Proring.

evidence.quote: You can do the Ice cave now if you want to, but this is the absolute hardest cave in the game, because many of the enemies use RUB and other related auto-kill attacks and you do not have a Proring at this time to prevent them.

facts.subject: Red Gargoyle
facts.text: Red Gargoyles appear in packs of 3-6 and repeatedly cast FIR2 for 20 to 40-50 damage, making AFIR or fleeing advisable.

evidence.quote: You will find some Red Gargoyles, these will cause you problems no matter what you do.  They cast FIR2 almost incessantly, and have pretty high attack power too.  Just use AFIR as soon as you encounter them...And, to top it off, they usually travel in packs in 3-6 and usually get the first attack.  FIR2 can do as little as 20 damage, or as much as 40-50...Just run if you see any.

facts.subject: Fire
facts.text: Players cannot run from the Fire monster, which only attacks and can be defeated with ICE2.

evidence.quote: Also, there is a monster called Fire.  He looks and acts much like Earth.  He can't do anything but attack, but, like Earth, he does that very well.  Fire can be a threat to your characters if they have low HP and/or defense.  You can't run, so just attack and use ICE2 if you want.

facts.subject: Perilisk
facts.text: Cockatrices use SQUINT to turn targets to stone, while accompanying Perilisks have an instant kill attack, and both can be defeated with ICE2.

evidence.quote: Also in the Gurgu Volcano, you will find Cockatrices, who will use SQUINT on you and turn you to stone.  There will also be Perilisks that hang out with them.  These guys will use something like squint, I forget what it's called, but it will kill you instantly.  Just use a blast of ICE2 and you will find any Cockatrices and Perilisks paying you big bucks for killing them.

facts.subject: Gurgu Volcano
facts.text: A Flame shield can be found on the first couple floors of Gurgu Volcano.

evidence.quote: On the first couple floors, you won't find much, except maybe a Flame shield (or is that lower?).

facts.subject: Gurgu Volcano
facts.text: The Giant Sword is found in Gurgu Volcano and is intended to give an edge against Giants.

evidence.quote: You will also find the Giant Sword, which is supposed to give you an edge against Giants, but most any other sword you have by this time will do much better than the Giant Sword.

facts.subject: Gurgu Volcano
facts.text: The Ice Sword found lower in Gurgu Volcano provides an extra boost against fire enemies.

evidence.quote: As you get lower, you will find a MUCH better weapon, the Ice Sword.  This is a Fighter or Red Mage's pride and joy.  This will be the most powerful weapon for them for a LONG time.  It seems to have an extra boost against fire enemies, but it doesn't seem at all ineffective against Ice enemies for some reason.

facts.subject: Gurgu Volcano
facts.text: Flame Equipment found in Gurgu Volcano provides good defense for Fighters and protects against Ice attacks.

evidence.quote: You will also find some Flame Equipment which will provide good defense overall for a Fighter and will protect against Ice attacks.

facts.subject: Agama
facts.text: Heading west on the bottom lava level of Gurgu Volcano leads to a candle-enclosed treasure chest preceded by a square spiked with Agama.

evidence.quote: To start, head west (left), but only if you dare.  You will find yourself in a room with candles enclosing a treasure chest.  Just before you enter this little "cage", you will find a square spiked with Agama.

facts.subject: Agama
facts.text: Agama on spiked squares uses HEAT for 20-30 damage, provides good Exp, and can be defeated in one round.

evidence.quote:
I guess you should note Agama also.  He can use a 
move called HEAT, which is pretty much like FIR2, except it only does about 20-
30 damage to your party.  There are a few spiked squares with Agama.  I 
recommend fighting, because he gives you some good Exp.  Plus, he has fairly low 
HP and Defense, so with a full-party attack, you should be able to knock him off 
in one round.

facts.subject: Red Dragon
facts.text: Red Dragon casts BLAZE for 50-80 damage to all party members, which AFIR reduces to 20-40 damage.

evidence.quote:
He can use BLAZE, which is like FIR3.  This does about 50-80 damage to every 
single member of your party.  Use AFIR immediately to reduce this to 20-40 
damage per character (still, ouch).

facts.subject: Red Dragon
facts.text: Red Dragon's physical attack deals about 30-90 damage.

evidence.quote:
His attack isn't quite as dangerous, but 
provides no relief.  He can do about 30-90 damage, much depending on who he's 
attacking.

facts.subject: Gurgu Volcano
facts.text: Defeating the Red Dragon rewards the party with the Flame Armor.

evidence.quote:
So, get your prize, the Flame Armor, and proceed East back to where you started 
on this level.

facts.subject: Kary
facts.text: Kary has around 600 HP and can hit 6 or 7 times in an attack, making INV2, RUSE, or INVS crucial.

evidence.quote: You should also have your White Wizard use Inv2 or the White Shirt for the same affect. This will help reduce damage done to you by the wild amounts of hits which Kary can get.

HP-600?...Kary can get lots of 
hits on you, sometimes up to 6 or 7, so make sure you use INV2 plenty of times 
if you have it, or at least use RUSE or INVS on your weak ones.

facts.subject: Kary
facts.text: After defeating Kary, placing the ORB on the altar and exiting through the portal purifies the Fire Crystal.

evidence.quote:
Well, Kary should vanquish sooner or later, and when she does, put the ORB 
on the alter and exit through the portal.

facts.subject: Sorcerer
facts.text: Sorcerers in the Ice Cave deal 1-2 damage with physical attacks that inflict instant-death RUB.

evidence.quote:
Also in the Ice Cave are Sorcerers, who will cause you much pain.  
They do little other than attack, and when they do, they only do about 1-2 
damage.  However, the kicker is that they have RUB in their attack.

facts.subject: Frost Wolf
facts.text: Frost Wolves attack in packs of up to 6 and use FROST for up to 60 ice damage, requiring AICE for defense.

evidence.quote:
Their attack is mild, but 
they have a move called FROST, which causes Ice-based damage.  It can easily do 
up to 60 damage without AICE, and multiplied by 6 Frost wolves WILL cause 
problems.

facts.subject: Ice Cave
facts.text: The left treasure chest in the pit room of the Ice Cave contains the Flame Sword.

evidence.quote:
You will see 
3 treasure chests, partially surrounded by a number of holes.  Go to the one on 
the left, without stepping on any of the holes.  You will get a Flame Sword, 
which will help you with undead and Ice monsters.

facts.subject: Ice Cave
facts.text: The right chest in the pit room contains Cloth and is guarded by dangerous Mages.

evidence.quote:
Do NOT get the chest on the 
right!!!  It is guarded by several Mages who will probably wipe you out.  The 
chest only contains Cloth, such a waste.

facts.subject: Ice Cave
facts.text: A room on the left side of the Ice Cave contains the Ice Armor.

evidence.quote:
After 
you get out of the room, you can go to the left side and find a room with the 
Ice Armor.

facts.subject: Ice Cave
facts.text: A room at the bottom-left of the Ice Cave contains 8 treasure chests filled with GP, with a spiked square of Frost Wolves at the end.

evidence.quote:
room with 8 treasure chests filled with TONS of GP.  There is a spiked square 
with Frost Wolves at the end, so watch out.

facts.subject: Eye
facts.text: The Eye has around 150 HP and uses instant-kill attacks including RUB, petrification Glance, XXXX, and Brak.

evidence.quote: The Eye has 162 HP and can use XXXX, BRAK, RUB, and other instant death spells... You'll get 3225 EXP (divided among surviving characters) and 3225 GP.

Eye- HP about 150 or so...He will start off using RUB or similar 
spell, which will most likely knock one of your guys out right away....He can also use 
Glance, which will turn you to stone.  He also uses many auto-kill spells like 
XXXX and Brak.

facts.subject: Ice Cave
facts.text: Defeating the Eye guarding the middle chest allows obtaining the FLOATER.

evidence.quote: Where Found: | Find inside the Ice Cave.

This time, you can get the chest in the middle.  But before you can get to the 
chest...Yay!! You get the FLOATER!

facts.subject: Airship
facts.text: Using the FLOATER inside the desert raises the Airship.

evidence.quote:
All the way on the bottom right corner of the 
island, you will see a desert....Use the FLOATER you got from the 
Ice Cave.  Watch in awe as the Airship appears before your very eyes!

facts.subject: Castle of Ordeal
facts.text: Entering the Castle of Ordeal courage test requires the CROWN.

evidence.quote:
As 
you enter, you will see a man that tells you that you need a CROWN to take the 
courage test (God knows why you COULDN'T have the CROWN at this point in the 
game).

facts.subject: Castle of Ordeal
facts.text: To solve the teleporter maze, use the sofa, go right to the first teleporter, then right and up, choose the bottom teleporter, go left and down, choose the bottom teleporter, follow the hall, choose the bottom-right teleporter, and take the top hallway.

evidence.quote:
Make your way to the room on the upper left and jump in the sofa.  Here, 
you are in a room, and outside you will notice some column-shaped teleporters.  
Go out of the room and to the right to the first teleporter.  Then, right and up 
to the next one.  Now, you will have a choice.  If you pick the right one, 
you'll move on, but if you pick the wrong one, you'll teleport back to somewhere 
you were before.  Go into the bottom one.  Then, hook left and down into the 
next teleporter.  Next, you will have a choice again.  Take the one on the 
bottom.  Follow the little hallway to the next teleporter and go in.  Then, you 
will have another choice.  Take the one on the bottom right, closest to you.  
Here comes the biggest choice of all.  You will be at the beginning of 2 large 
hallways.  Take the one on top.

facts.subject: Castle of Ordeal
facts.text: A chest guarded by a Mud Golem holds the Zeus Gauntlet, which can be selected as an item during battle to cast LIT2 infinitely at no MP cost.

evidence.quote:
There will 
be a treasure chest there.  The square next to it is spiked with a Mud Golem....You will get a 
Zeus Gauntlet for winning....In battle, go to ITEM, and select the Zeus Gauntlet and hit A.  It will 
cast LIT2 in battle.  What's better?  It doesn't use up ANY magic points and you 
can use it an INFINITE number of times!

facts.subject: Castle of Ordeal
facts.text: After leaving the Zeus Gauntlet room, skip the teleporter directly below and take two steps right, then walk down the hallway into the correct teleporter.

evidence.quote:
Directly 
below you is a teleporter, but do NOT take it.  Take two steps to the 
right, and go down the hallway.  There will be a teleporter right below you as 
you walk straight down.  This is the one you want.

facts.subject: Castle of Ordeal
facts.text: Past the Nightmares spiked square, chests above contain a Heal Staff, which casts HEAL in battle to restore HP to everyone.

evidence.quote:
As 
soon as you step into the room, there will be a spiked square with Nightmares 
(cousins or MadPony)....Kill them, and get the treasure chests above you.  
Among other things, you will find a Heal Staff.  
Much like the Zeus Gauntlet, you can use the Heal Staff in battle to cast HEAL 
and restore some HP to everyone.

facts.subject: Castle of Ordeal
facts.text: Moving to the left in the upper treasure area reveals an Ice Sword and a Gold Bracelet.

evidence.quote: Head to the left, and you will find and Ice Sword and a Gold Bracelet.

facts.subject: Castle of Ordeal
facts.text: The Castle of Ordeal contains a treasure chest holding the TAIL to the right near a sofa.

evidence.quote: The first two warp podiums aren't too hard to manuver past since they are straight forward, after that take the bottom warp podium and collect the Zeus Guantlet and head to the third floor and then go around and pick up the rest of the treasure chests and the Tail.
The tail is found near the end of...the Castle.
Anyway, go to the right, and you will see a treasure chest and a sofa.  Get the treasure chest from the bottom.  It's the TAIL!!!

facts.subject: Zombie Dragon
facts.text: Zombie Dragon attacks physically and can be defeated using regular attacks and Harm spells.

evidence.quote:
Contrary to most bosses,  
Zombie D can't do anything other than attack, and that he doesn't even do that 
well.  Rather than use tough boss strategy, just attack and use Harm spells.

facts.subject: Bahamut
facts.text: Bahamut is located on the Cardia Islands in the bottom-right hole on the forest-covered island with 2 holes.

evidence.quote:
He is located on the Cardia 
Islands, which is a rather simple maze.  To get to him, find the island with 2 
holes that's covered with forest.  His hole is on the bottom right of this 
island.

facts.subject: ProRing
facts.text: ProRings can be purchased in Gaia to protect characters against RUB and similar spells.

evidence.quote:
First, head to Gaia.  That's the town 
in the upper right corner of the map, surrounded by mountains, northeast of the 
Mirage Desert.  You should buy ProRings for everyone, as they prevent RUB and 
like spells.

facts.subject: Lost L8 Magics shop
facts.text: A semi-secret passage through a notch in the upper right town gates of Lefien leads to two shops selling the Level 8 spells LIF2 and NUKE.

evidence.quote:
As if it's a big secret, there is a semi-secret 
passage in Lefien that leads to the 2 "best" magic spells in the game.  If you 
go to Lefien, go to the upper right section of town.  There will be a notch in 
the town gates for you to walk through.  Go to the right to find 2 small shops 
right next to each other... The LOST L8 MAGICS!  The White side has LIF2 and the 
Black Side has NUKE.

facts.subject: CUR4
facts.text: The Level 7 White Wizard spell CUR4 restores HP to maximum as long as the recipient is not stoned or dead.

evidence.quote:
Well, the White Wizard 
will definitely want CUR4, which you've been waiting the whole game for.  
This spell restores your HP to the Max, no questions asked as long as you're not 
stoned or dead.

facts.subject: ICE3
facts.text: The Level 7 spell ICE3 can deal up to 240 damage to all enemies.

evidence.quote:
Well, ICE3 is 
really nothing new, only it's very powerful.  I think it can do up to 240 damage 
to all enemies, and even more than that if they're weak against it.

facts.subject: LIF2
facts.text: The Level 8 White Wizard spell LIF2 revives a dead warrior to full health.

evidence.quote: LIF2 will revive a dead warrior to full health, no questions asked.

facts.subject: FADE
facts.text: The White Wizard spell FADE can deal up to a little over 300 damage per monster and hits any enemy.

evidence.quote:
FADE is an excellent spell.  It can do up to a little over 300 damage per 
monster, and unlike HARM, works on any enemy, not just undead.

facts.subject: NUKE
facts.text: The Level 8 Black Wizard spell Nuke can deal up to 400 damage.

evidence.quote:
Nuke packs a mean punch up to 400 damage, but I thought that's what 
your Knights and Masters were for.

facts.subject: Eye
facts.text: Defeating the Eye rewards 3228 Experience and 3228 GP.

evidence.quote: He will give you 3228 Experience and GP, the EXP of course divided amongst the survivors.

facts.subject: Eye
facts.text: The Eye can use Glance to turn characters to stone, which can be blocked completely by equipping a Ribbon.

evidence.quote: He can use Glance and turn you to stone. However, he seldom uses it, and it usually doesn't work anyway. If it's still a problem, equip a Ribbon to block it completely.

facts.subject: Eye
facts.text: Fighting the Eye repeatedly is a fast and safe way to grind to level 50 and reach the maximum amount of 999,999 GP.

evidence.quote: Anyway, this way is quicker and safer than any other way I know to get up to level 50 and get the maximum amount of money, 999,999 GP.

facts.subject: Loot Root
facts.text: The Loot Root sequence gets key treasures early by going to Castle of Ordeal for the tail, skipping Volcano to get FLOATER from Ice Cave, raising Airship, getting CUBE from Waterfall, looting Sea Shrine top floors and B1-B2 after OXYALE, getting SLAB and CHIME, clearing Mirage Tower/Sky Castle and Tiamat, and finally killing Kraken and Kary.

evidence.quote: After you get the canoe, head over to the Castle of Ordeal and get the tail...Skip the Volcano, and get the FLOATER from the Ice Cave...Get the Airship, and buy stuff you need...Pick up stuff from the Waterfall and get the CUBE...Pick up stuff from the top 2 floors of the Sea Shrine, then floor B1 and B2, after getting the OXYALE from the fairy...Learn Lefienish with the SLAB and get the CHIME...Get the stuff from the Mirage Tower/Sky Castle and kill Tiamat...Kill Kraken, then Kary.

facts.subject: Mirage Tower
facts.text: Mirage Tower contains the ADAMANT used to forge Excalibur.

evidence.quote: If you don't want to, head straight to the Mirage Tower to get the treasures there like the ADAMANT for Xcalbur.

facts.subject: Waterfall
facts.text: Entering the Waterfall treasure room triggers a spiked square battle yielding about 4000 GP against combinations of Wizard Mummies, Mummies, Cockatrices, and Perilisks.

evidence.quote: Now, as soon as you enter the treasure room, there will be a spiked square filled with undead monsters. You'll find combinations of mainly WzMummies and Mummies mixed with a couple Cockatrices and maybe a couple Perilisks...Each battle yields about 4000 GP, which will quickly add up to enough to buy at least one Level 8 Magic Spell or another Gold Bracelet.

facts.subject: Waterfall
facts.text: Talking to the robot in the Waterfall rewards the CUBE needed to enter the Sky Castle.

evidence.quote: First, talk to the robot to get the CUBE, which you need to get into the Sky Castle, but you won't need that for a while.

facts.subject: Waterfall
facts.text: A treasure chest in the Waterfall contains the Defense sword, which casts RUSE when used in battle.

evidence.quote: First, there is the Defense sword, which is the third best weapon for the Red Wizard, besides the Sun Sword, and the Masmune, of course, neither of which you have at this point. The Defense sword casts RUSE in battle.

facts.subject: Waterfall
facts.text: A treasure chest in the Waterfall contains the Wizard Staff, which casts CONF in battle and can be sold for 25,000 GP.

evidence.quote: You will also find the Wizard Staff. This is relatively useless, so you can sell it for 25,000 GP. If you don't need the cash, you can keep it, as it casts CONF when used in battle.

facts.subject: Waterfall
facts.text: A treasure chest in the Waterfall contains a Ribbon, an equippable helmet for any class that provides resistance to all elements including poison attacks.

evidence.quote: Now, the grand finale! There's a Ribbon in here! The Ribbon equips as a helmet, accessible to any class...First, it provides resistance to all the elements including poison-based attacks, such as Gas D and Tiamat's POISON.

Waterfall Cave is basically just a long series of blocky intersections with a treasure room located at the southwest corner. Walking through the door will result in a fight with a mob of annoying but individually weak enemies which you can blast with spells at your leisure; the room contains 6 chests (Wizard Staff, Ribbon, 13450 G, 6400 G, 5000 G, Defense sword).

facts.subject: Oasis
facts.text: The shop at the Oasis sells a BOTTLE for 50,000 GP.

evidence.quote: The guy there will sell you a BOTTLE for 50,000 GP.

facts.subject: Gaia
facts.text: After using the BOTTLE to release the fairy, talking to her in the northeast corner of Gaia rewards the OXYALE.

evidence.quote: Go to the item menu and use the BOTTLE. It will tell you that a fairy popped out, then is gone. Now, go back to Gaia. All the way in the northeast corner of the town, you will find the fairy waiting for you there. Talk to her, and she will give you OXYALE.

facts.subject: Water
facts.text: Waters in the Sea Shrine can deal 90+ damage to a Knight and are weak to Ice spells.

evidence.quote: Monster:    | Water ... Weaknesses: | Ice
Water           300                                      Ice

What little damage you do manage will still be a small chunk out of their high HP. Yet, they have a nasty bite (or however the hell a little swirl can really hurt you), and can easily do 90+ to a well-armored Knight. Use Ice for these little pricks.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine
facts.text: The top floor of the Sea Shrine contains Opal equipment and the SLAB needed to learn the Lefeinish language.

evidence.quote: On the top floor with all the Mermaids (where most of the Mermaids are), you will find the Opal equipment, and the SLAB, which you must give to Dr. Unne in Melmond to learn the Lefeinish language, which will be important later.

facts.subject: Sea Shrine
facts.text: The bottom section of the Sea Shrine contains the Opal Armor, two Light Axes, the Mage Staff, and a Ribbon.

evidence.quote: Now, we head to the bottom. You will find the Opal Armor, as well as 2 Light Axes, the Mage Staff, and a Ribbon.

facts.subject: Light Axe
facts.text: Using Light Axes in battle casts HRM2, while the Mage Staff casts FIR2.

evidence.quote: The Light Axes will be very useful against the undead as they cast HRM2. The Mage Staff will also be good against the undead, as it casts FIR2.

facts.subject: Kraken
facts.text: Kraken has 600 HP and is weak against lightning.

evidence.quote: HP-600...He does cast LIT2/3 sometimes (seems odd seeing as he's weak against it), and that can hurt.

facts.subject: Kraken
facts.text: Kraken can hit 8 times for over 400 damage, so defense should begin with 2 to 3 layers of INV2, followed by ALIT for LIT3, and FAST on attackers.

evidence.quote: Cast Slow on Kraken and cast Fast on your fighters and if Kraken uses Ink, use Lamp(if you have it) to counteract the effects.

He will be able to get 8 hits on you at once, and nail you for over 400 damage sometimes, enough to send a White/Black Wizard or a weak Master to the floor in a hurry....Since his attack is clearly the biggest threat, start with 2-3 layers of INV2 to help reduce his attack power.  After about 3 shots of INV2, the biggest threat now will be LIT3.  Cast ALIT to nullify the danger of that.  Follow that up by FASTing your warriors, then continue with INV2 and healing.
Kraken's game-plan is very simple: 75% of the time he will use a regular attack, 25% of the time he will use Ink to try and blind your party.

facts.subject: Dr. Unne
facts.text: Taking the SLAB to Dr. Unne in Melmond allows the party to learn the Lefeinish language.

evidence.quote: To save you the effort of coming here in vain, take the SLAB to Dr. Unne in Melmond.  He will teach you the Lefeinish language.

facts.subject: Magic shop
facts.text: A secret magic shop in the upper-right section of Lefein sells NUKE and LIF2.

evidence.quote: If you didn't figure it out by now, or you didn't know already, there is a secret Magic shop in the upper-right part of town....Find the notch in the gate and head to the right to get NUKE and LIF2.

facts.subject: Lefein citizen
facts.text: Talking to the person in the bottom left corner of Lefein yields the CHIME used to unlock Mirage Tower.

evidence.quote:
After a long walk south to Lefein, and talk to
the people. They'll tell you of the Floating Castle, the Sky Warriors, and of
Tiamat. One will give you the CHIME, which is the key to the Mirage Tower.
However, all you really need to do is go to the top, head right, down, and talk to the guy standing still on the bottom left corner.  He will give you the CHIME to unlock the Mirage Tower.

facts.subject: Chimera
facts.text: Chimeras use BLAZE for fire damage and are weak against Ice.

evidence.quote: You will also see Chimeras.  They will use BLAZE on you (or something to that effect), which will cause Fire damage....They are weak against Ice if you are inclined to use magic.

facts.subject: Mirage Tower 1F
facts.text: The first floor of Mirage Tower contains the Thor Hammer, which casts LIT3 when used in battle.

evidence.quote: Head into the treasure room on the first floor where you'll find some interesting yet simple mazes to get tons of cool treasure....You will also find the best weapon (save the Masmune) for the White Wizard, the Thor Hammer.  You can actually hurt an enemy with this if you Attack (unlike other hammers), or USE it to cast LIT3, a great choice for undead or sea creatures.

facts.subject: Sky Castle 1F
facts.text: The first floor of Sky Castle contains the Bane Sword, which casts BANE when used in battle.

evidence.quote: As you progress up to the first floor of the Sky Castle, you will find the Bane Sword among other things.  The Sword itself is rather weak, but it casts BANE in battle, which will wipe out a whole group of enemies provided it works.

facts.subject: Sky Castle 2F
facts.text: The southwest branch of Sky Castle 2F contains ADAMANT, which can be given to the dwarf blacksmith in Dwarf Cave to forge Excalibur.

evidence.quote: On the next floor, you will find the ADAMANT on the southwest branch, which you need to give to the Dwarf Blacksmith in the Dwarf Cave (as if you couldn't figure out where it was) to get the Xcalbur, the best weapon that the Knight alone can use.

facts.subject: Sky Castle 2F
facts.text: The southwest corner of Sky Castle 2F contains the White Shirt, which casts INV2 when used in battle.

evidence.quote: On the southwest corner, you will find the White Shirt, which only the White Wizard can equip, which he should....This wonder-cotton blouse casts INV2 when you USE it in battle, which is one of the most useful defensive spells in the game.

facts.subject: Sky Castle 2F
facts.text: Beside the White Shirt is a black-dyed shirt that casts ICE2 when used in battle.

evidence.quote: Right next to this treasure chest is another White Shirt, only this time dyed black, and is complementary color Wizard.  The magic black dye in here causes ICE2 to be cast in battle when USEd instead of INV2.

facts.subject: Sky Castle upper floor
facts.text: An upper treasure floor of Sky Castle contains a Katana.

evidence.quote: One more level up, you will find some second-rate treasure compared to what you got before....Other things on this floor include more second-rate stuff and a Katana, the ideal weapon for the Ninja.

facts.subject: Mirage Tower teleporter
facts.text: Entering Sky Castle through the teleporter in Mirage Tower requires the CUBE.

evidence.quote: Head up to the teleporter.  You can't get through here unless you have the CUBE.  You will now be in the sky castle.

facts.subject: Sky Castle maze room
facts.text: In the looping grid maze floor of Sky Castle, move right 2 spaces and up 2 spaces to reach the teleporter.

facts.subject: WarMech
facts.text: A party with a Fighter and two Red Mages can defeat WarMech using support spells like INV2, ARUB, FOG2, FAST, and CUR3.

evidence.quote: It can hit for about 200-400 even on a Knight, and it uses Nuclear, which hits for about the same or even more on the whole party. To make matters worse, it usually gets the jump on your party, well being a machine its to be expected, and it uses Nuclear about 85-90% of the time first thing, so if you are not healed, it could quite easily wipe out your party before you know what hit you.
The firepower of the Fighter and 2 Red Mages really can knock out a WarMech no problem when combined with the support of INV2, ARUB, FOG2, FAST, and CUR3 from your Mages.

Warmech also has a pair of extremely accurate physical attacks that hit harder than even Chaos' and has a 25% chance to blast your party with a slightly buffed version of the Black Wizard's Nuke spell, potentially hitting for over 300 AOE non-resistable damage.

facts.text: Matoya's Cave contains three chests with two Heal potions and a Pure potion.

evidence.quote: If you cross the bridge and keep heading straight north until you can't anymore, you'll bump into Matoya's Cave, which contains 3 chests with a Heal potion, another Heal potion, and a Pure potion.

facts.subject: Peninsula of Power
facts.text: Winning a battle on the Peninsula of Power must be done before talking to Bikke and his pirates in the top left corner of Pravoka.

evidence.quote: This must be done before talking to Bikke and his two pirate buddies in the top left corner of the town of Pravoka (earning Pirate Bay [achievement 3570]). The Peninsula of Power is an area reached by walking south of Pravoka, east through the mountain pass, turning north as soon as you can, and then continuing north past the boat dock until you reach the edge of the landmass.

facts.subject: ZomBull
facts.text: The two grass tiles on the Peninsula of Power spawn high-level Lefein enemies, including the ZomBull which has 224 HP and a weakness to fire.

evidence.quote: The two grass tiles at the very end of this peninsula have bugged encounter data and contain enemies from the Lefein area that you are meant to encounter much later in the game. You'll want to use a Tent or other saving item before walking on those tiles, as many of the potential encounters on the Peninsula of Power are highly dangerous. The encounter you're most likely to make it out alive from is a single ZomBull, which is blessedly not that uncommon; exploit its weakness to fire if possible and hope you get through its 224 HP before it finishes chewing through your team with its melee attacks.

facts.subject: Dwarf Cave
facts.text: Two chests near the entrance of the Dwarf Cave contain 450 G and 575 G.

evidence.quote: Most of the chests here are locked away until you have the magic key, but you can open two near the entrance for 450 G and 575 G.

facts.subject: Ship
facts.text: Holding A and pressing B 55 times while on the ship triggers a 15-block sliding puzzle minigame that awards 100 G.

evidence.quote: Holding A and then pressing B 55 (fifty-five) times while on the ship will trigger a sliding puzzle minigame to occur. There are 15 blocks with numbers on them, and your goal is to slide them until they've been sorted into order. Successfully do so, and you'll get 100 G and this achievement.

facts.subject: Elfland graves
facts.text: Interacting with the graves north of the inn in Elfland triggers an easter egg.

evidence.quote: The southern port you can access with the ship at this point will drop you off in the vicinity of Elfland. Go into the town and head around north of the inn to happen on some graves; interact with them to find an easter egg.

facts.subject: Marsh Cave
facts.text: Four chests on the northern side of the second floor of the Marsh Cave contain 680 G, a Large Knife, a Short Sword, and 620 G.

evidence.quote: The northern side of the second floor has 4 chests (680 G, Large Knife, Short Sword, 620 G); the south part of the floor has a few empty chests inside the rooms.

facts.subject: Marsh Cave
facts.text: The third floor of the Marsh Cave contains six chests holding Iron Armor, 295 G, a Copper Bracelet, a House, 385 G, and the Crown.

evidence.quote: The third floor has 6 non-empty chests you can open at this point, including Iron Armor, 295 G, Copper Bracelet, House, 385 G, and a **required chest** (in the room down 3 rows and right 1 column from the entrance stairs) containing the CROWN.

facts.subject: Magic key
facts.text: Defeating Astos with the Crown yields the Crystal, which is traded to Matoya for the Herb to awaken the Elfland prince and receive the magic key.

evidence.quote: Speaking of locked rooms, once you've taken the Crown to Astos and defeated him, you can trade off the Crystal he dropped to Matoya, who will give you the Herb, which will wake up the prince of Elfland [achievement 3571] to give you the magic key.

facts.subject: Elfland Castle
facts.text: A locked room in the top-right corner of Elfland Castle contains four chests holding a Silver Hammer, 400 G, 330 G, and a Copper Gauntlet.

evidence.quote: Starting with the Elfland region, walking around the outside edge of the castle to the top-right corner of the map will lead you to a locked door containing 4 chests (Silver Hammer, 400 G, 330 G, Copper Gauntlet).

facts.subject: Northwest Castle
facts.text: A locked room in Astos' castle northwest of Elfland contains three chests holding a Power Staff, a Falchon, and an Iron Gauntlet.

evidence.quote: Making your way back to Astos' castle northwest of Elfland will allow you to crack open a room with several forced encounter tiles and three more chests (Power Staff, Falchon, Iron Gauntlet).

facts.subject: Marsh Cave
facts.text: Three locked chests along the south edge of the third floor of the Marsh Cave contain a Silver Bracelet, a Silver Dagger, and 1020 G.

evidence.quote: Marsh Cave:  Silver Bracelet, Silver Knife, 1020 gold
The northern side of the second floor has 4 chests (680 G, Large Knife, Short Sword, 620 G); the south part of the floor has a few empty chests inside the rooms.

The third floor has 6 non-empty chests you can open at this point, including Iron Armor, 295 G, Copper Bracelet, House, 385 G, and a **required chest** (in the room down 3 rows and right 1 column from the entrance stairs) containing the CROWN.

After cleaning out Elfland castle and the northwest castle, the Marsh Cave isn't too far off, and we can now grab the last three chests along the south edge of the third floor (Silver Bracelet, Silver Dagger, 1020 G).

facts.subject: Coneria Castle
facts.text: The locked rooms in Coneria Castle contain an Iron Armor, Iron Shield, and TNT in the left room, and an Iron Staff, Sabre, and Silver Dagger in the right room.

evidence.quote: The left locked room in Coneria Castle contains three chests (from left to right: Iron Armor, Iron Shield, **TNT**-which you must obtain to progress). The right room contains another three chests (Iron Staff, Sabre, Silver Dagger).

facts.subject: Temple of Fiends
facts.text: Locked rooms in the top-right and bottom-right corners of the Temple of Fiends contain three chests with a Were Sword, a Soft potion, and a Rune Sword.

evidence.quote: Temple of Fiends:  Rune Sword, Were Sword, Soft Potion
As soon as you enter the Temple of Fiends to the northwest of Coneria, you can find 3 chests on the left corners of the main floor, which contain a Cap, a Cabin, and a Heal potion.
Unlock the doors in the top right and bottom right corners of the temple for a total of 3 chests (Were Sword, Soft potion, Rune Sword).

facts.subject: Dwarf Cave
facts.text: The locked south chamber of the Dwarf Cave contains eight chests with a Cabin, Iron Helmet, Dragon Sword, Silver Dagger, Wooden Helmet, Silver Armor, 575 G, and a House.

evidence.quote:
Dwarf Cave:  Cabin, Iron Helmet, Dragon Sword, Silver Knife, Wooden Helmet,
 Silver Armor, House, 575 gold
The Iron Helmet is worth keeping if you've got a Fighter, but sell everything else. The Silver Armor is much more expensive than Iron, but it's also a lot weaker.
Most of the chests here are locked away until you have the magic key, but you can open two near the entrance for 450 G and 575 G.
The south chamber of the Dwarf Cave is locked; opening it up reveals a bounty of 8 chests (Cabin, Iron Helmet, Dragon Sword, Silver Dagger, Wooden Helmet, Silver Armor, 575 G, House).

facts.subject: Dwarf Cave
facts.text: Talking to the dwarf in the Dwarf Cave with TNT opens a new sea passage to Melmond and the Earth Cave.

evidence.quote: Talking to the nearby Dwarf while in possession of TNT will result in a new sea passage being opened, meaning you can now sail to Melmond and the Earth Cave.

facts.subject: Of Mighty Magic
facts.text: Mastering Of Mighty Magic in one run requires starting with at least one White Mage or Black Mage, as Red Mages cannot learn any level 8 spells and will max out at 20 spells learned.

evidence.quote: If you are aiming to master the set in one run, Of Mighty Magic [achievement 27656] means that starting with at least one party member as a White Mage or Black Mage is a hard requirement; Red Mages cannot learn any level 8 spells and will max out at 20 spells learned even after their class upgrade.

facts.subject: Kraken
facts.text: Kraken has 800 HP, resists Fire and Earth, is weak to Lightning, attacks 8 times, and is neutral to Cold, Status, Poison, Time, and Death.

evidence.quote:
Boss: Kraken

HP: 800
Weakness: Lightning
HP-600...He does cast LIT2/3 sometimes (seems odd seeing as he's weak against it), and that can hurt.
Kraken statistics: 800 HP, weak to Lightning, neutral to Cold, Status, Poison, Time, and Death, resists Fire and Earth; attacks hit 8 times

facts.subject: Kraken
facts.text: Kraken uses a regular attack 75% of the time and Ink 25% of the time to try and blind the party.

evidence.quote: Kraken's game-plan is very simple: 75% of the time he will use a regular attack, 25% of the time he will use Ink to try and blind your party.

facts.subject: One for Each Arm
facts.text: Spells targeting the whole party count as one action for each target affected during the Kraken 8-action challenge.

evidence.quote: It should also be noted early on that due to the logic of the challenge, casting spells that target your whole party will count as one action for each target affected - don't go pressing Inv2 or Hel2 here.

facts.subject: Kraken
facts.text: Lit3 can inflict up to 360 damage per cast against Kraken, though roughly 200 damage is more typical.

evidence.quote: Lit3 can potentially do up to 360 damage per cast, though somewhere in the 200 range is more likely.

facts.subject: Kraken
facts.text: Kraken has 60 Absorb, making high-level offensive magic or Fast-buffed physical attacks key strategies.

evidence.quote: Lit3 can potentially do up to 360 damage per cast, though somewhere in the 200 range is more likely.

Depending on your party composition, beating Kraken with raw physical damage may not be ideal; if you have some Wizards to work with, high level offensive magic may be more of a core strat, since Kraken's 60 Absorb is making the Knight's good old fashioned Silver Sword look a bit outdated.

facts.subject: Of Mighty Magic
facts.text: White Wizards can finish learning 24 spells in Gaia with Fade and Wall, while Black Wizards can purchase any two 8th level spells there.

evidence.quote: _Have a character learn 24 spells._ ... White Wizards can run back to Gaia and fill in the rest of their slots with Fade and Wall (Xfer doesn't do anything when cast); Black Wizards can do the same with any two of the 8th level spells there (you're most likely not going to do anything with them either way).

facts.subject: Mirage Tower
facts.text: Mirage Tower is located in the desert northwest of Lefein, reached by landing the airship on grass to the south and walking.

evidence.quote:
find a place to land your airship inside the mountain range
that encircles a huge desert. You'll find the Mirage Tower in the middle of
the desert
Mirage Tower's located in the vast desert northwest of Lefein and you'll have to land the airship on a small patch of grass to the south then walk the rest of the way in order to get there.

facts.subject: Floor 1
facts.text: The interior of Mirage Tower Floor 1 contains 8 chests holding a Cabin, Aegis Shield, 2750 G, 3400 G, 18010 G, Vorpal sword, Heal Helmet, and 880 G.

evidence.quote: After entering Mirage Tower, there are 8 chests accessible in the interior of floor 1 (Cabin, Aegis Shield, 2750 G, 3400 G, 18010 G, Vorpal sword, Heal Helmet, 880 G).

facts.subject: Floor 1
facts.text: In Mirage Tower Floor 1, stairs leading up to Floor 2 are situated across the wall from the entrance.

evidence.quote: The stairs up to Floor 2 are just across the wall from the entrance.

facts.subject: Floor 2
facts.text: To reach the stairs and treasure room on Mirage Tower Floor 2, go counterclockwise around half the room and weave through the pillar rows.

evidence.quote: You'll have to make it through a bit of a pillar maze upon entering Floor 2; getting to the stairs and the treasure room requires going counterclockwise around half the room, then weaving your way through the rows of pillars to get to the interior of the floor.

facts.subject: Thor's Hammer
facts.text: Thor's Hammer is found in the middle-left chest inside the treasure room in the middle of Mirage Tower Floor 2.

evidence.quote: Found in the treasure room in the middle of Floor 2 of the Mirage Tower; it's the middle-left chest, specifically.

facts.subject: Floor 2 treasure room
facts.text: The remaining chests in Mirage Tower Floor 2 treasure room contain 13000 G, 12350 G, 7900 G, 8135 G, Dragon Armor, 10000 G, Sun Sword, 7690 G, and a House.

evidence.quote: After that specific treasure, crack open the rest in this floor 2 treasure room (13000 G, 12350 G, 7900 G, 8135 G, Dragon Armor, 10000 G, Sun Sword, 7690 G, House).

facts.subject: Floor 3
facts.text: Mirage Tower Floor 3 contains a teleporter leading to the Floating Castle, which requires the Cube to operate.

evidence.quote: Floor 3 doesn't actually have anything on it besides a teleporter that goes up to the Floating Castle and requires the Cube to operate (hopefully you have it; if not, it's in the Waterfall Cave near Onrac).

facts.subject: Floor 1 west room
facts.text: Floating Castle Floor 1 west treasure room contains 4 chests with 9900 G, Heal potion, 4150 G, and 7900 G.

evidence.quote: Teleporting to the first floor of the Floating Castle, there's a treasure room to the west (4 chests, 9900 G, Heal potion, 4150 G, 7900 G), a treasure room to the east (5 chests, 5000 G, ProRing, 6720 G, Heal Helmet, 180 G), and a treasure room to the south (1 chest, Bane Sword).

facts.subject: Floor 1 east room
facts.text: Floating Castle Floor 1 east treasure room contains 5 chests with 5000 G, ProRing, 6720 G, Heal Helmet, and 180 G.

evidence.quote: Teleporting to the first floor of the Floating Castle, there's a treasure room to the west (4 chests, 9900 G, Heal potion, 4150 G, 7900 G), a treasure room to the east (5 chests, 5000 G, ProRing, 6720 G, Heal Helmet, 180 G), and a treasure room to the south (1 chest, Bane Sword).

facts.subject: Floor 1 south room
facts.text: Floating Castle Floor 1 south treasure room contains 1 chest holding the Bane Sword.

evidence.quote: Teleporting to the first floor of the Floating Castle, there's a treasure room to the west (4 chests, 9900 G, Heal potion, 4150 G, 7900 G), a treasure room to the east (5 chests, 5000 G, ProRing, 6720 G, Heal Helmet, 180 G), and a treasure room to the south (1 chest, Bane Sword).

facts.subject: Floor 1
facts.text: The teleporter leading to Floor 2 of the Floating Castle is located to the north.

evidence.quote: The teleporter to Floor 2 is up north.

facts.subject: Floor 2 northwest room
facts.text: The northwest room of Floating Castle Floor 2 contains 2 chests holding a Silver Helmet and a House.

evidence.quote: Floor 2 is laid out like a compass; northwest is a room containing 2 chests (Silver Helmet, House).

facts.subject: Floor 2 west room
facts.text: The west room of Floating Castle Floor 2 contains 2 chests holding 880 G and 13000 G.

evidence.quote: West contains 2 more chests (880 G, 13000 G).

facts.subject: Floor 2 southwest room
facts.text: The southwest room of Floating Castle Floor 2 contains 1 chest holding the Adamant.

evidence.quote: Southwest contains 1 chest (Adamant).

facts.subject: Floor 2 southeast room
facts.text: The southeast room of Floating Castle Floor 2 contains 2 chests holding a Black Shirt and a White Shirt.

evidence.quote: Southeast has 2 chests (Black Shirt, White Shirt).

facts.subject: Floor 2 east room
facts.text: The east room of Floating Castle Floor 2 contains 2 chests holding an Opal Shield and a Ribbon.

evidence.quote: East has 2 chests (Opal Shield, Ribbon).

facts.subject: Floor 2 northeast room
facts.text: The northeast room of Floating Castle Floor 2 contains 1 chest holding an Opal Gauntlet.

evidence.quote: Northeast contains 1 chest (Opal Gauntlet).

facts.subject: Floor 2
facts.text: Directly south from the starting teleporter on Floating Castle Floor 2 is the teleporter to Floor 3.

evidence.quote: Directly south from the starting teleporter is the teleporter to Floor 3, which has a couple standalone tasks to deal with right away.

facts.subject: God's Eye View
facts.text: Upon teleporting to Floor 3, speak to the nearby green robot and examine the hole at the bottom of the rectangular window.

evidence.quote: As soon as you teleport up to Floor 3, you can talk to the green robot nearby and then examine the hole in the bottom of the rectangular "window" to get this bit of text.

facts.subject: Floor 3 left-hand room
facts.text: A Katana is located in the furthest right chest of the 4 chests in the left-hand path treasure room on Floating Castle Floor 3.

evidence.quote: Found in the treasure room along the left-hand path from where you got the previous achievement; there's 4 chests, it's the one furthest to the right.

facts.subject: Floor 3 left-hand room
facts.text: The remaining three chests in the Floor 3 Katana room contain a Soft potion, 4150 G, and 3400 G.

evidence.quote: Continuing on from the room where we just grabbed the Katana, there's three other chests in there (Soft potion, 4150 G, 3400 G).

facts.subject: Floor 3 north room
facts.text: The north room from the Floor 2 teleporter on Floating Castle Floor 3 contains 4 chests with 9000 G, Heal potion, ProRing, and 5450 G.

evidence.quote: Heading back to the teleporter from Floor 2 and going north this time, there's another room with 4 chests (9000 G, Heal potion, ProRing, 5450 G).

facts.subject: Floor 3 east wing room
facts.text: The east wing treasure room on Floating Castle Floor 3 contains 6 chests with 6400 G, Cloth, ProCape, Soft potion, 9500 G, and 8135 G.

evidence.quote: This floor's east wing has one more treasure room containing 6 chests (6400 G, Cloth, ProCape, Soft potion, 9500 G, 8135 G).

facts.subject: Floor 3
facts.text: The teleporter leading up to Floor 4 is located under the room where the Katana was found.

evidence.quote: Go up to Floor 4 via the teleporter under the room where you got the Katana.

facts.subject: Floor 4
facts.text: On Floating Castle Floor 4, travel east past one grid intersection, then head south at the second intersection to reach the Floor 5 teleporter.

evidence.quote: Floor 4 is massive but also empty; go east past one grid intersection, then once you reach a second intersection head south to find the Floor 5 teleporter.

facts.subject: Warmech
facts.text: Warmech has a 4.7% chance of spawning as a random encounter on Floor 5 of the Floating Castle.

evidence.quote: Floor 5 of the Floating Castle has a 4.7% chance of spawning a Warmech as a random encounter.

facts.subject: Warmech
facts.text: Warmech has 1000 max HP, 80 absorb, 100% magic evade, resists every element except Time (7% chance to hit with Stop and 0% chance with Zap!).

evidence.quote: This creature is something of a bonus boss; its 1000 max HP and 80 absorb make it bulkier than any boss you've seen thus far and it resists every element except Time (you have a 7% chance to hit it with Stop and a 0% chance to hit it with Zap!, so that defensive gap isn't doing much)...Considering its ridiculous offense and 100% magic evade, the main strategy here is to buff up a physical attacker and hope they can kill it before it kills you.

facts.subject: Warmech
facts.text: Warmech has accurate physical attacks and a 25% chance to cast a buffed Nuke doing over 300 non-resistable AOE damage.

evidence.quote: Warmech also has a pair of extremely accurate physical attacks that hit harder than even Chaos' and has a 25% chance to blast your party with a slightly buffed version of the Black Wizard's Nuke spell, potentially hitting for over 300 AOE non-resistable damage.

facts.subject: Tiamat
facts.text: Tiamat has 1000 HP, 100% magic evade, is weak to Poison, neutral to Status, Time and Death, resists Fire, Cold, Lightning, and Earth, and attacks hit 4 times.

evidence.quote: Tiamat statistics: 1000 HP, weak to Poison, neutral to Status, Time and Death, resists Fire, Cold, Lightning, and Earth, attacks hit 4 times...She has 100% magic evade and is neutral to Status, so most spells that inflict status ailments won't reasonably work.

facts.subject: Tiamat
facts.text: Tiamat has a 50% chance of attacking and a 50% chance of cycling special attacks that deal Lightning, Poison, Cold, and Fire damage in order.

evidence.quote: I would have your White Wizard put up Alit and Aice, as Tiamat uses both the Thunder and Blizzard attacks... In the second round, have your Red and White Wizard use Inv2 to help avoid with Tiamat's physically hits which are decent as far as monster damage goes.

HP-1000...He has some nasty auto-kill attacks, so equip ProRings beforehand or cast ARUB.  He also has a THUNDER attack, a nasty move that's like LIT3, only more powerful.  He can also use POISON a nasty damaging attack....He has 50 defense like WarMech, so only high level fighters will beuseful for hand/sword-to-whatever-he-has.
Tiamat has a 50% chance of attacking you and a 50% chance of cycling through a set of special attacks that do Lightning, Poison, Cold, and Fire damage, in that order.

facts.subject: Tiamat
facts.text: The Bane spell or Bane Sword has around a 20% chance of instantly killing Tiamat due to her Poison weakness.

evidence.quote: Tiamat is weak to Poison, which makes it *possible* for the spell to connect, but not terribly likely - the chance of any given cast connecting is around 20%...The Bane Sword's use effect is exactly as likely to hit as the black magic spell and you can use it unlimited times per fight; you also don't need to be able to equip it to cast Bane with it.

facts.subject: Excalibur
facts.text: Delivering the Adamant from the Floating Castle to the blacksmith in the Dwarf Cave yields the Excalibur.

evidence.quote: If you got the Adamant from the chest in the Floating Castle, deliver it to the blacksmith in the Dwarf Cave and he'll whip up the Excalibur for you.

facts.subject: Temple of Fiends (Past)
facts.text: Touching the black orb in the Temple of Fiends near Coneria after defeating all four fiends sends the party to Temple of Fiends (Past).

evidence.quote: After defeating all four fiends, a black orb will manifest in the Temple of Fiends near Coneria; touching it will send you back to the Temple of Fiends (Past).

facts.subject: Floor 3
facts.text: From the start on Floor 3 of Temple of Fiends (Past), head to the bottom right corner to find stairs leading to Floor 2.

evidence.quote: You start the Temple of Fiends (Past) on Floor 3. No chests here, aim for the bottom right corner of the floor and take the stairs to Floor 2.

facts.subject: Floor 2
facts.text: The interior chamber of Floor 2 has stairs leading up to Floor 1.

evidence.quote: This small interior chamber has another set of stairs leading up to Floor 1.

facts.subject: Floor 1 central room
facts.text: The central room on Floor 1 contains two chests holding 45000 G and 65000 G.

evidence.quote: Head to the central room of this floor to find two chests (45000 G, 65000 G), then use the Lute on the stone plate to uncover a ladder leading down.

facts.subject: Floor 1 stone plate
facts.text: Using the Lute on the stone plate in the Floor 1 central room uncovers a ladder leading down to the main part of Floor 2.

evidence.quote: Head to the central room of this floor to find two chests (45000 G, 65000 G), then use the Lute on the stone plate to uncover a ladder leading down. The ladder will drop you off in the main part of Floor 2; make tracks for the northwest corner of this floor to get back to Floor 3, then take the path heading west to find another set of stairs down leading to Floor 4.

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Follow the path along the outside of Floor 4 to reach the southeast corner and refight Lich to proceed to Floor 5.

evidence.quote: Nothing useful on Floor 4, follow the path along the outside of the floor to reach the southeast corner and refight Lich to proceed down to floor 5.

facts.subject: Floor 5 south doors
facts.text: On Floor 5, the left door leads to two chests with a ProRing and a Katana, while the right door leads to two chests with a ProCape and 26000 G.

evidence.quote: Don't approach the stairs yet, take the path south to reach a pair of doors. The left one leads to two chests (a ProRing and a Katana), the right one leads to another two chests (ProCape, 26000 G).

facts.subject: Kary
facts.text: Approaching the stairs down on Floor 5 triggers a refight with Kary before proceeding to Floor 6.

evidence.quote: Afterwards, retrace your steps to the stairs down, approach them to refight Kary, and make it down to floor 6.

facts.subject: Kraken
facts.text: The southeast corner of Floor 6 contains the Kraken refight leading to Floor 7.

evidence.quote: Floor 6 has no treasures to worry about and making your way through is just a matter of navigating the rooms with multiple doors; your goal and the Kraken refight are in the southeast corner of the floor.

facts.subject: Masamune
facts.text: Masamune is found on Floor 7 by heading south then east through the boxy rooms and following the corridor extending from the southeast room's southeast corner.

evidence.quote: Pick this up on Floor 7 of the Temple of Fiends (Past). From the entry stairs, head south and then east through a couple of the boxy rooms; you'll see a corridor extending from the southeast corner of the southeast room. Follow it to pick up the Masamune, then take out Tiamat again and move down to Floor 8.

facts.subject: Chaos
facts.text: Chaos has 2000 HP, 100% magic resistance, resists all elements, attacks twice per turn, and can inflict non-elemental paralysis.

evidence.quote: Chaos Statistics: 2000 HP, Resistant to All Elements, Attack hits twice, Attack can inflict paralysis (non-elemental)...Chaos has a 100% magic resistance on top of his full suite of elemental resists, so offensive magic is suboptimal here.

facts.subject: Chaos
facts.text: Chaos has a 25% chance of physical attacks, 25% chance of special attacks (Crack, Inferno, Swirl, Tornado), and 50% chance of cycling spells (Ice3 -> Lit3 -> Slo2 -> Cur4 -> Fir3 -> Ice2 -> Fast -> Nuke).

evidence.quote: Chaos has a 25% chance of attacking you physically, a 25% chance to use a special attack from a list of Crack (Earth-elemental instant KO), Inferno (heavy fire magic damage to all allies), Swirl, and Tornado (identical non-elemental full party magic attacks, not as much raw power as Inferno but can't be resisted), and a 50% chance of cycling through a spell list of Ice3 -> Lit3 -> Slo2 -> Cur4 -> Fir3 -> Ice2 -> Fast -> Nuke.

facts.subject: Chaos
facts.text: Chaos is fully repeatable, allowing players who beat him without optional items to return and defeat him without healing on a second run.

evidence.quote: It should be noted that Chaos is technically a fully repeatable fight, and a run that beat him without picking up any optional items will have a considerable victory lap to mastery anyway since they will have to go clear out every dungeon (including the Temple of Fiends). If you find that you need healing to win in the no-optional-chests fight, you can go back and do this after your collecting spree, putting a pretty fitting cap on your mastery.

facts.subject: Earth Cave 1F

evidence.quote: the first floor contains 5 chests (1975 G, Pure potion, 795 G, 880 G, Heal potion).

facts.subject: Earth Cave 1F

facts.subject: Earth Cave 2F

evidence.quote: Floor 2 of the Earth Cave contains another 6 chests split between two treasure rooms (Coral Sword, Cabin, 330 G, 5000 G, Wooden Shield, 575 G).

facts.subject: Earth Cave 3F
facts.text: Floor 3 of the Earth Cave includes four chests before the boss room containing a Tent, Heal potion, 3400 G, and 1020 G.

evidence.quote: The lowest floor we can access right now is floor 3, which includes four chests before reaching the boss room (Tent, Heal potion, 3400 G, 1020 G)

facts.subject: Earth Cave 3F
facts.text: A required chest located in the left corner of Vampire's room on floor 3 contains the Ruby.

evidence.quote: and one additional **required** chest which can be opened after beating Vampire (the one in the left corner of Vampire's room; contains **Ruby** required to proceed further).

facts.subject: Titan
facts.text: Talking to Titan in Titan's Tunnel with the Ruby in your possession clears him out of the way.

evidence.quote: Talking to Titan with the Ruby in your possession will clear it out of the way.

facts.subject: Titan's Tunnel
facts.text: The south chamber of Titan's Tunnel contains 4 chests holding a Silver Helmet, 450 G, 620 G, and Great Axe.

evidence.quote: The treasure chests in the cave contain a Great Axe and a Silver Helmet for your fighter.

facts.subject: Sarda
facts.text: Talking to the sage in Sarda's Cave grants the Rod.

evidence.quote: Take the other exit out of Titan's Tunnel now, head down to Sarda's Cave, and talk to the sage to get the Rod.

facts.subject: Earth Cave 3F
facts.text: Taking the Rod back to Earth Cave unlocks the stone slab accessible from the right exit of Vampire's room on floor 3, allowing descent to floor 4.

evidence.quote: Taking the Rod back to the Earth Cave will unlock the weird slab accessible from the right exit of Vampire's room on floor 3. You can now proceed down to floor 4

facts.subject: Earth Cave 4F
facts.text: Floor 4 of the Earth Cave features two treasure rooms with 8 chests: the top room has 5450 G, 1520 G, a Wooden Staff, 3400 G, and 1455 G, while the southwest room has 1250 G, a Silver Shield, and a Cabin.

evidence.quote: floor 4, which has two treasure rooms and a total of 8 chests (top treasure room: 5450 G, 1520 G, Wooden Staff, 3400 G, 1455 G; southwest treasure room: 1250 G, Silver Shield, Cabin).

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Lich has 400 HP, is weak to Fire and susceptible to Harm spells, neutral to Lightning and Earth, resistant to Ice, Status, Poison, and Death, and can inflict Paralysis with physical attacks.

evidence.quote: Lich statistics: 400 HP, Weak to Fire, Susceptible to Harm spells, Neutral to Lightning and Earth, Resistant to Ice, Status, Poison, and Death, physical attacks can inflict Paralysis (Fire-elemental)

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Lich has a 25% chance of using a physical attack and a 75% chance of casting magic, following a set spell order of Ice2 -> Slp2 -> Fast -> Lit2 -> Hold -> Fir2 -> Slow -> Slep.

evidence.quote:
Lich is the first fiend so he is of course the weakest of the four.  However,
he does have a fairly good attack power (he can stun the person he attacks),
spells like Ice2 (hits your entire party) and Slep (can knock members out of
the fight for a while), and he can land multiple hits as well.  That being
said, Lich is classified as undead, so Fire and harm spells will slaughter
his Hit points (therefore he can die from one blast each of Fir3 and Hrm3).

Have your Mages go all out and cast Fire and Harm, leaving your
weapon users to remove meager amounts of Hit Points (Lich DOES have a high
Absorb rating), OR have your Red Mage and Black Mage cast Fast on the
weapon users to take him down physically

Mute does not work on him; he's too powerful.  So, 
instead, cast your anti-elemental spells (Aice, Alit, Afir) to significantly 
decrease the damage done by his attack spells.  You should also use Fast on your 
fighters so they can inflict more damage on Lich.  Your Mages should never 
attack because they will only do 1 damage.
HP-400 I think...Also, LICH will use FIR2 and ICE2, so make sure you use AFIR and AICE to help out a bit.
Nintendo Power says that LICH is weak against Fire, but even FIR3 will never do more than 40-50 damage, so don't bother with that.
Lich has a 25% chance to spend its turn using a physical attack and a 75% chance of casting a spell.... Lich's spell list is Ice2 -> Slp2 -> Fast -> Lit2 -> Hold -> Fir2 -> Slow -> Slep.

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Lich most likely casts Ice2 on turn one dealing 80 to 160 damage without resistance, which can be mitigated if a White Magic user casts AIce before Lich acts.

evidence.quote: What this means for you is that Lich will most likely spend its first turn casting Ice2, which can deal anywhere from 80 to 160 damage if you don't resist it.... If you have access to level 4 white magic, you can try casting AIce immediately to cut in front of Lich and grant your party ice resistance, but you'll be gambling on your white magic user getting to go before Lich does.
White magic users can cast ALit upon seeing Fast to significantly reduce the damage of the upcoming Lit2.

If you brought a White Mage, dropping a Hel2 after the initial Ice2 is probably a good idea, but outside of that your efforts should mainly be focused on making sure Lich is dead before it gets around to casting something dangerous again. Black magic users who can cast Fir3 should consider buying the spell here; a high roll from Fir3 can take out over half of Lich's health in one cast, and even a low roll does a significant chunk. The White Mage's Hrm3 is also capable of solid results and probably the best thing they could be doing if the party is at high health.
Fighters and Black Belts may have trouble with Lich's physical defense at this point; having Fast cast on them can help to fish for critical hits.

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: White magic users can cast ALit upon seeing Lich cast Fast to significantly reduce the damage of the upcoming Lit2 spell.

evidence.quote: White magic users can cast ALit upon seeing Fast to significantly reduce the damage of the upcoming Lit2.

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Dropping a Hel2 after Lich's initial Ice2 is recommended for White Mages, while casting Fir3 or Hrm3 deals massive damage to defeat Lich quickly.

The White Mage's Hrm3 is also capable of solid results and probably the best thing they could be doing if the party is at high health.

facts.subject: Lich
facts.text: Casting Fast on Fighters and Black Belts helps overcome Lich's physical defense by fishing for critical hits.
